David Sear.bio: David Sear (b. 1932) is a folk singer and radio host. He enrolled at Black Mountain College to record African American folk music in the area. In New York, he formed a partnership Dillingham & Sear to tune and repair pianos, clavichords and harpsichords. His group, the American Folk Trio, brought folk music to children through the YoungAudiences programs mostly in the New York area, but also throughout the United States. He had a program, Adventures in Folk Music, on WNYC in which he combined folk and Baroque music. He later changed the title to Folk Music Almanac. He also ran a folk music concert series at the Spencertown Academy in Spencertown, New York.

Willem \"Bill\" de Kooning.bio: One of the most prominent and celebrated of the Abstract Expressionist painters, Willem de Kooning's pictures typify the vigorous, gestural style of the movement. Perhaps more than any of his contemporaries, he developed a radically abstract style of painting that fused Cubism, Surrealism and Expressionism. While many of his colleagues moved from figuration to abstraction, de Kooning always painted figures, most notably women, and abstractions concurrently, making no distinction between the art historical categories. De Kooning's real subject, he insisted, was space and the figure-ground relation. De Kooning fused abstraction, figuration, and landscapes in various ways throughout the many long decades of his career, and his unceasing journey to find new forms and subjects made his overall output more eclectic than most of his colleagues. His engagement with popular culture was also unique and informed a host of post-war artists from the Neo-Dadaism of Robert Rauschenberg to the Pop Art of James Rosenquist, and younger painters such as Cecily Brown have explored the gestural eroticism of his later paintings.

Margaret \"Peggy\" Clapp.bio: Margaret attended BMC from the spring to fall of 1940. Before attending, she was enrolled in the Anne Hastings' Dramatic School. Her transcripts weren't saved, but faculty notes share that she was mostly interested in her drama coursework and fell behind in other subjects.

Mary Cullis.bio: Mary was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

Henry \"Hal\" Adams, Jr..bio: Henry "Hal" Bethune Adams, Jr. was active at the College, giving weekly news commentaries to the study body and participating in many drama events. Henry’s senior examination records and some of his class writings are in his student file and show his love for writing. He joined the student body in the fall of 1942 and was drafted in 1943. While in the service, he regularly sent updates to the Community bulletins of his time away. Though there isn't much information accessible to share facts of his life while a student or shortly after, one can see that he had a love for storytelling when looking through the College bulletins. He even mentions in one that he was writing articles, essays, and fiction, and hoping to have someone look over his work. Henry returned to complete his senior evaluations at BMC until 1947. He requested transfer records from the college to be sent to the University of Chicago, University of Michigan, Duke University, and Harvard University in 1949. He wrote to the college in 1951 from Durham, NC so it is assumed that he attended Duke University for his MA. He asked for another round of transcripts to be sent in 1953 to Washington University, University of Kentucky, Purdue University, and the University of Buffalo where he wished to continue in the study of Psychology.

Claire Rubel.bio: Claire Rubel was a student in fall 1945. While a student, she participated in student concerts as a violinist.

Elmer Hall.bio: James Hall was twenty-three when he enrolled at Black Mountain for the fall of 1940. After graduation from Lyndhurst High School in New Jersey, he had worked at various jobs while saving enough money for one semester at Louisiana State University.

Robert Turner.bio: Robert Chapman Turner was an American potter known for his functional pottery, sculptural vessels and inspired teaching. Born in Port Washington, New York, Turner attended Swarthmore College and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1936. He then studied painting at the Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Arts and earned a Master of Fine Arts degree from the New York State College of Ceramics at Alfred University in 1949.

Kenneth Chorley, Jr..bio: Kenneth attended the Summer Art Institute of 1951. He shared in his application that he was working as a cabinetmaker and was interested in taking courses in color and design. Herminio Portell Vilá.bio: Herminio Portell Vilá was a Cuban writer and scholar and faculty of history at BMC from fall 1935 to spring 1938.

Ruth Bailey.bio: Ruth Bailey was an assistant teacher in art at Black Mountain College from September 1936 to February 1938.

Kathleen Gardner.bio: Kathleen Gardner was kitchen and/or maid staff for at least the 1944 school year.

Sue Thomas Turner.bio: Sue Turner (1913-2009) came to Black Mountain College with her husband Robert Turner, who had been hired to create a ceramics program at the college. At BMC, she took a course in theater with Wes Huss, but her primary focus was on caring for her two small sons. Sue Turner was an active supporter of Quaker values in public education. The Sue Thomas Turner Quaker Education Fund was established in her honor.

Edward \"Jimmie\" Jamieson.bio: Edward Jamieson was a student from 1938 to 1942. While a student, he was a student officer and participated in productions, A Doll's House and Waiting for Lefty.

Elizabeth \"Betty\" Kelley.bio: Betty Kelley was a student from 1940 to 1945 and was one of the few to graduate. She was the niece of faculty and rector, Robert Wunsch. She also married a fellow BMC student, Homer Bobilin and they lived in Black Mountain, NC after attending the college.

Milton \"Robert\" Rauschenberg.bio: Rauschenberg was an American painter and graphic artist whose early works anticipated the Pop art movement. Rauschenberg is well known for his Combines, a group of artworks which incorporated everyday objects as art materials and which blurred the distinctions between painting and sculpture.

Cliff Harmon.bio: Cliff F. Harmon studied at the Bisttram School of Fine Arts in Los Angeles and at the Taos Valley Art School in New Mexico. It was in Taos in 1948 that he met his wife Barbara Sayre (August 8, 1927 - ), also a student at the Bisttram School. They settled in Taos where they built their adobe house and studios.

Laille Schutz.bio: Laille Schutz was a student for the summer of 1944 where she took Weaving with Anni Albers.

Frances Goldman.bio: Frances was a student from fall of 1939 to spring of 1941.

Thomas \"Tommy\" Jackson.bio: T.R. “Tommy” Jackson was a student at Black Mountain College for the spring of 1951, the 1951-52 regular sessions, and the 1953 spring and fall sessions. He also attended the 1951 and 1953 summer programs. Jackson had attended the progressive Windsor Mountain School in Lenox, Massachusetts. He worked on various projects at the college under different names including the Black Mountain Engineers and the Black Mountain Sports Car Services.

Emma Kulan.bio: Elsa Kulan was a secretary at the college from mid-spring semester of 1946 to spring 1947. She shared in her application that she worked as a secretary-steno, receptionist, switchboard operator at Clifford and Lawton, Inc; Aeronautical Draftswoman at The Chance Vought Aircraft Corp, Secretary in export department at The Bermuda Shop, Executive secretary at Oppenheim Collins, and was currently working as Assistant Advertising Production Manager at The Ben Sackheim Advertising Agency Inc. at time of application to BMC.

Edith MacIntosh.bio: Edith MacIntosh was a librarian at the college from October 1939 to April 1940, while Mrs Rice was away for library school.

Hilda Terry.bio: Hilda Terry first studied with Josef Albers at a seminar in Groton, Massachusetts and then at Black Mountain in the summers of 1944 and 1945. At the time she was a student at Black Mountain, she was Assistant Curator in the Department of Architecture at the Museum of Modern Art in New York. She taught art at the Baldwin School in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania for twenty-five years.

Hope Greer.bio: Hope was a student for fall 1941 to spring 1942.

John Bailey, Jr..bio: John Malcolm Bailey, Jr was a student from the spring of 1946 to the spring of 1947. He was enrolled in the Army before coming to Black Mountain and while a student, he was a coordinator of the work program.

Doris Birtic.bio: Doris was a guest for the 1941 summer work camp.

Susan Brown.bio: Susan Brown was a student from the fall of 1943 to the spring of 1944. She left the school on a leave of absence to "marry an infantryman before he went overseas," and did not return. She instead took coursework at UCLA. (Susan's student file, letter from Susan Brown to Herbert A Miller, 10/4/1944)

Jane Mayhall.bio: Jane Mayhall was a student of music from fall 1937 to summer 1944. She attended the 1944 Music Institute. Before BMC she attended Louisville Girls’ High School 1933-1936.

Richard Weber.bio: Richard Weber was a student from 1950 to 1952. He also studied acting at the Carnegie Institute of Technology. He was a founder of the Beverly Hills Playhouse where he performed.

Zoya Sandomirsky.bio: Zoya Sandomirsky was a guest for the work camp in the summer of 1942. She received advanced degrees in sociology and in human development, and was a feminist psychologist and therapist. She was also active in human and civil rights and was Human Rights Commissioner in Boston.

Robert Fine.bio: Robert was a student for the summer of 1949. He was in the Army from 1954 to 1956.

Nancy Brager.bio: Nancy Brager Katz was born in Baltimore, Maryland August 31, 1916 to Mr. and Mrs. A. Stanley Brager. She attended Park School from 1930 to 1934 and earned a diploma. She then attended John Hopkins University Teacher’s College from 1934 to 1935. Brager was admitted to Goucher College in 1934 but 36 was unable to attend due to financial concerns.

Francis Drinker.bio: Francis Snow Drinker was guest faculty of music for the 1949 Summer Music Institute. He is listed as a flutist.

Ann Jameson.bio: Ann Jameson was a student for fall of 1936. Before BMC, she attended Smith College (1933-1935).

Roscoe \"Ross\" Penley.bio: Ross Penley was the farm manager (or often called the Superintendent of the Farm) from fall of 1940 to winter of 1946. Ross was accompanied by his wife, Stella, and their three children.

Sue McNeil.bio: Alice McNeil was a student for the 1943-44 school year. While a student, she served as a student officer and Heinrich Jalowetz was her advisor.

Kirill Chenkin.bio: Kirill Chenkin taught French and comparative literature at the college from 1939 to 1940.

Gloria Beckman.bio: Gloria June Beckman attended the 1944 Summer Art Institute. At the time of her application, she held a BA in fine art from Ohio State University and worked in painting, drawing, and sculpture.

Nancy Bernstein.bio: Nancy attended the 1945 Summer Art Institute. She previously attended Cornell University 1945-1949 and obtained a BA in fine art. She also attended the Syracuse University Summer School in 1944, Parsons School of Design throughout 1942-1945, Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture in Summer 1947, and Art Students League in Summer 1948. At the time of application, she listed employment as Assistant Department of Education, Museum of Modern Art.

Mary Dodge.bio: Mary Dodge attended the 1945 Summer Arts Institute, where she took Weaving with Anni Albers. She taught at Abbott Academy in Andover, Massachusetts.

Irma Wolpe.bio: Irma Wolpe Rademacher, née Schoenberg, was a Romanian-born American pianist and teacher. She taught music at BMC in the summer of 1953.

Lorna Blaine.bio: Lorna Blaine Howard Halper studied at Barnard College in New York before enrolling at Black Mountain College for the 1945 Summer Art Institute. She returned to the college in the winter of 1946 as a regular student and remained through the spring of 1948, except for the spring and summer 1947 terms. She studied with Josef Albers, Fannie Hillsmith, Robert Motherwell, Max Dehn and Ilya Bolotowsky, among others.

Irving Knickerbocker.bio: Irving Knickerbocker was faculty of psychology from fall 1935 to spring 1937. Dates unknown, but he was born in 1900.

John Urbain.bio: John Julian Arthur Urbain was born in Brussels, Belgium in 1920. He moved with his parents to Detroit in 1922. Urbain, one of a number of students from Cass Technical High School in Detroit to enroll at Black Mountain for the 1946 winter quarter on the suggestion of his friend and fellow student, Ray Johnson. He remained through the 1947 fall semester.

George Zabriske.bio: George Zabriskie taught writing at the college from the fall of 1944 to the summer of 1945. At the time of teaching at the colleg he held an A.B. from Duke University and authored "The Mind's Geography" while a Guggenheim fellow of poetry in 1942-43. Zabriskie went on to author many other books and collections of poems. There are many college bulletins that share his involvement in college activities, including weekly poetry readings for the students and faculty, and serving as fire chief on the Fire Committee. While chief, he did handle one large fire in 1944.

Bernice Bernstein.bio: Bernice Bernstein attended the college from the fall of 1945 to February of 1947. While a student at the college, Bernice took courses in economics, psychology, music, and literature and attended student run club, Modern Dance group.

Robert Orr.bio: Robert C Orr was guest faculty of accounting and economics from winter 1943 to spring 1944. He also served as the college treasurer/ business manager.

Raymond Trayer.bio: Raymond Trayer worked on the farm and with the work program from the fall of 1946 to the spring of 1951.

Elizabeth Gellhorn.bio: Elizabeth was a student from fall 1946 to fall 1947. After leaving BMC, Elizabeth worked for many years at the Stockbridge Library.

Maude Roundtree.bio: Maude Roundtree was staff at the college in 1944. She was listed under "kitchen or maid" staff lists.

Ellen Siegel.bio: Ellen Siegel taught weaving from fall 1949 to spring 1950. She also taught weaving at the Haystack Mountain School of Crafts.

Victor Sprague.bio: Victor Sprague, a marine biologist and authority marine invertebrates and their parasites, taught biology at Black Mountain from the fall of 1951 through the fall of 1952. Spague obtained his Ph.D. from the University of Illinois and taught at several schools including Louisiana State University and Young Harris College. He served in the army during World War II. Before arriving at Black Mountain, he was head of the Parasitology Division, Project 9 at the Texas A&M Research Foundation.

Jesse Green.bio: Jesse Dawes Green was born in Stanley, Wisconsin on February 9, 1928 to insurance agent Jesse Green and Arleva Cooper Green. He attended Stanley High School from 1942 to 1945 and was enrolled at the Robert Hutchins Great Books College, a special preparatory school, at the University of Chicago, from 1945 to 1946 where he received his high school certificate.

Robert Luntz.bio: Robert Luntz was a student in the fall of 1935 to spring of 1936.

Percy Baker.bio: Percy Hayes Baker was a scholar of the sciences and an educator. He taught biology at the North Carolina College from 1930 to 1934, then at the Virginia State College from 1934 to 1945, when he came to Black Mountain College. Baker was awarded a grant from the Julius Rosenwald Fund to work at Virginia State College on the study of the preparation of school texts in science in 1937 (Chattanooga Daily Times, 3 May, 1937).

Doris Tentchoff.bio: Doris Tentchoff was a student from 1943 to 1944. While a student, she was a member of the international relations club.

Lucille \"Chris\" Blaha.bio: Lucille was a student at the college for fall 1950 but left during the semester. After leaving BMC, she enlisted in the Air Force to during WW2.

Henry Jaeger.bio: Henry Hastings Jaeger was a student for the 1946 Music Institute and stayed on until spring 1947. While at the college, he participated in the Prehistoric Specimen football team.

Bacia Stepner.bio: Bacia Stepner Edelman was born in Boston, Massachusetts and attended Black Mountain College in the summer of 1946, studying design under Josef Albers and sculpture under Concetta Scarvaglione and Leo Amino.

Martha Rittenhouse.bio: Martha Rittenhouse first read about Black Mountain College in Readers’ Digest (the condensed version of Louis Adamic’s article “Education on a Mountain”). Although she and her parents were interested in the college, after high school she enrolled at Bridgewater College in Virginia.

Harold Anderson.bio: Harold Henry Anderson was a student at Black Mountain College for the fall semester of 1945. A recommendation letter from Mr. Erbie Bunten, of the Muskegon Public School system, shared that Harold was socialistic and an avid reader. He also shared that his family was religious and very active in the church, but that Harold held more scientific views. He had an interest in architecture and design. He was admitted as a student in the fall of 1945 and asked for a withdraw by mid-October.

Ralph Chernoff.bio: Ralph was a student for the fall of 1947 and left during the fall semester of 1948. He took coursework in German, Mathematics, Physics, and Philosophy. After leaving BMC, he attended the University of Illinois. He also wrote back to the college in 1956 to share that he was serving in the Army and planned to enroll at the University of California upon discharge.

Irene Schawinsky.bio: Irene Schawinsky was faculty of art, often listed as "tutor" in dress design, from 1936 to 1938.

Peter Julian.bio: Peter Julian was a student in the summer of 1953 to study dance.

Sadiee Whitfield.bio: Sadie Whitfield was office staff from April to August of 1946.

Lino Bartoli.bio: Lino Bartoli gave lecture recitals on the development of the piano-violin sonata and lead string ensembles at the college for the summer of 1947. Mr. Bartoli was formerly first violinist with the Pittsburg Symphony, and concert master of both the Pittsburg Opera Company and the Pittsburg String Sinfonietta.

Anne \"Nan\" Chapin Weston.bio: Anne "Nan" Howard (Chapin) Weston (1913-1992), a native of Hartford, Connecticut, was a student at Rollins College, Winter Park, Florida, from 1930 to 1933. She, and her future husband, Norman Betts Weston (1913-2000), were among the body of students who followed John Andrew Rice from Rollins to Black Mountain College in Black Mountain, N.C., in the autumn of 1933.

Kathryn \"Kitty\" Carlisle.bio: Kathryn Carlisle was a student from fall of 1943 to spring of 1944.

Margaret Jackson.bio: Margaret Jackson (b. 1934) held several jobs: printing at New York University and taxi driver, among others. In Vermont, she worked simultaneously as a taxi driver, driver of a senior transport van (she eventually had her own business), school bus driver, and driver for the University of Vermont (eventually working exclusively for the University).

Mary \"Mickey\" Miller.bio: Mickey Miller (1927-2001) received her B.A. from the University of California-Los Angeles. While at Black Mountain College in the fall of 1947, she collected folk songs in the area. Those songs are included in a recording titled Mickey Miller Sings American Folk Songs (Folkways Records FA 2393) (accompanied by Beth Lomax Hawes). She obtained her master’s degree in psychology and was instrumental in forming of the Topanga Center for Human Development.

Barbara \"Bobbie\" Dreier.bio: Like her husband, Barbara Loines Dreier was from a family of nonconformists, "un-regular" Christians," and adventurous thinkers. Her great-grandmother had fone to China on a clipper ship with an aunt and uncle and had stayed for five years. Her grandmother was a suffragist and a Unitarian, which Bobbie Dreier recalled "was as good as being a Communist in her day," and she married a Quaker, who was "read out of meeting for marrying such a radical girl." Two of her aunts became Christian Scientists, and her mother left the Episcopal Church after becoming interested in theosophy.

Tasker Howard, Jr..bio: Tasker Howard, Jr. attended Rollins College, majoring in physics, and Antioch College, majoring in economics. He then attended BMC from 1936 to 1937 and graduated in June 1937 with a focus in economics.

Robert Tucker.bio: Robert Tucker was a student in 1948.

John Keith.bio: John Keith was founding faculty of romance languages, from fall 1933 to spring 1934. He held a PhD and studied and taught French and German. His recommendation letters share that he was a tutor at Harvard and Radcliffe.

Fiola Shepard.bio: Fiola Shepard taught French and German linguistics from fall 1949 to spring 1954.

Anna Moellenhoff.bio: Anna Moellenhoff (1892-1982) was faculty of biology and German from fall 1935 to spring 1939. Prior to coming to the college, Anna and Fritz worked as physicians in Germany.

Leonard \"Lenny\" Billing.bio: Leonard Winter Billing was a student from the fall of 1938 to the fall of 1941, then guest faculty for the 1951-1952 school year. He focused on architecture and woodworking. He also served as the Work Program Director. Leonard took Introductory Weaving with Anni Albers and Don Page in the Fall 1940 and Summer 1941, until he was drafted.

John Reiss.bio: John Reiss was a student from the Summer Art Institute of 1944 to winter 1946. Before BMC he attended Mesmer High School and Milwaukee State Teachers College. He also served in the Army in World War II.

Denver Gillen.bio: Denver Gillen (1914-1975) was an artist, whose work is now in collections across the country. Denver was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

Katharine Gilbert.bio: Katharine Gilbert was an a philosopher who studied aesthetics, and one of the first women to be president of the American Philosophical Society. She was also the first female professor at Duke University and, during her lifetime, the only female chairman of a liberal arts department.

Anne Arthur.bio: Anne entered as an older student, 32 at the time of submitting her application in 1942. She was interested in coming to Black Mountain because her husband visited the college and "couldn't stop talking about it." She was interested in learning more about art and music and participating in community life. She attended from the fall of 1942 to spring of 1943.

Henny Freud.bio: dhHenny Freud was guest faculty of French for the summer of 1943. She also attended the 1944 Summer Art Institute. Her application to the institute shares that she attended the State Academy of Fine Arts in Berlin and Dusseldorf, and listed her occupation as "housewife, some teaching, some painting."

Ernest Kennedy.bio: Ernest Kennedy was a student in fall of 1950.

Katherine Swartzbaugh.bio: Katherine Swartzbaugh was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

Nevalie Ropp.bio: Nevalie Ropp was a student from 1938 to 1940. She took Introductory Weaving with Anni Albers in Fall 1938 and Spring 1939.

Lucile Hall.bio: Lucile Hall was a student for the spring of 1936.

Naomi Doniger.bio: Naomi was a student from fall 1939 to spring 1940.

Julia \"Judy\" Hull.bio: Judy Hull was a student from 1939 to 1940. Before BMC, she attended Wellesley College (1938-1939).

Richard Bogart.bio: Richard Bogart was a student at the college, but no course cards were saved and dates attended are unknown. He attended the University of Illinois and served in the Navy before applying to BMC.

Anna Jessen.bio: Anna Jessen was a student from 1949 to 1950.

William Russell.bio: William Foster Russell was a student from 1934 to 1936.

Dora Schwarz.bio: Dora Schwarz was listed as faculty family and dietician for the 1945 school year.

Helen Tuttle.bio: Helen Tuttle was a student in 1941. She was an artist and educator.

Jeanne Karstens.bio: Jeanne Karstens was a student for the 1944 Summer Music Institute.

Cora Ward.bio: Cora Kelley was a student for the summers of 1949 and 150, and also worked as a nurse at BMC. She also attended the Newcomb Art School at Tulane University, Hunter College where she obtained an MA, and the Institute of Design in Chicago in 1953. In 1955, she moved to New York and became an active part of the second generation of Abstract Expressionists. After living in New York, she became active in Louisiana and much of her work was donated to the Paul and Lulu Hilliard University Art Museum of Louisiana.

Doris Woodward.bio: Doris Woodward was a student in spring of 1944.

Stanley \"Stan\" Cooke.bio: Stanley Cooke was a student at the college from fall 1948 to spring 1949. He was a veteran and attended on the GI bill. He noted in his application that he was interested in learning how to compose his own music. Mary Emma Harris wrote this bio for the BMC Project, "Later in New York he took classes at the Contemporary School of Music with Stefan Wolpe and Ralph Shapey and studied briefly at the Juilliard School. After leaving New York City, he worked in a factory as a toolmaker. He later became a computer programmer. He was a data processing manager and he lived in upstate New York."

Horace \"Mac\" Wood.bio: Horace McGuire Wood came to Black Mountain College (Black Mountain, NC) in 1942 to become the school's business manager and director of the work experience program. He later taught design and construction courses. After they left the college in December 1945, Mr. and Mrs. Wood continued to live at their home in the town of Black Mountain, where he conducted a house planning and building seminar for many years. (Biographical note taken from the finding aid for the Horace McGuire Wood Papers, 1933 - 1972, North Carolina State Archives.)

Richard \"Dick\" Lockwood.bio: Richard Lockwood was a student from winter 1945 to spring 1946.

Mary Beaman.bio: Mary Stacy Beaman was a student at the college from the fall of 1934 to the spring of 1936. She served as a Student Officer and on the Board of Fellows. Mary wrote in her application to the college that she was interested in "music, persian art, early French, [and] psychology."

Abraham \"Remy\" Charlip.bio: Remy Charlip was a guest of Lou Harrison in 1951 for Thanksgiving, and a student for the 1952 and 1953 summer sessions.

Robert Hartzler.bio: Robert was a student from 1943 to 1944.

Richard Lischer.bio: Richard Lischer was guest faculty of furniture design in the summer of 1948. He also attended a Weaving class with Anni Albers and Trude Guermonprez while at the college.

Nathaniel \"Nat\" French.bio: Nathaniel was a student from fall of 1933 to spring of 1936. Before BMC, he was a student at Rollins College. While a student, he served as a student officer. He left the school in June 1936 with honorable dismissal then approached faculty in January 1941 to take his Senior exam, the faculty approved his request in February and Nat returned to BMC Thanksgiving 1941 to take a series of 7 exams. He graduated on November 24, 1941.

Mary Lou \"Mel\" Mitchell.bio: Mary Lou Mitchell was a student for the 1949-1950 school year.

Hugo Kauder.bio: Hugo Kauder was a mid-century Viennese composer, pedagogue, and émigré to America, who defied the atonal trend of his generation with his uniquely harmonic, contrapuntal style. His legacy of over 300 works, many yet to be published, is receiving renewed interest today. -

He served as the first curator of the department of photography at the Museum of Modern Art and the second director of the George Eastman Museum. His book The History of Photography remains one of the most significant accounts in the field and has become a classic photographic history textbook.

Judith Davidoff.bio: Judith Davidoff was an American viol player, cellist, and performer on the medieval bowed instruments. She was considered the “Grande Dame of the viol”, "a master of the viola da gamba and other stringed instruments" and "a central part of the early-music scene."

Leah Portell Vilá.bio: Leah Portell Vilá was a Spanish tutor in the spring of 1947. She accompanied her husband Herminio to the college for his tenure spanning from fall 1935 to spring 1938.

Laurence \"Larry\" Birns.bio: A former defense researcher, strategist and member of the Institute for Strategic Studies in London and the All Souls College, Oxford’s military seminar, he was a senior grade public affairs officer of the U.N. Economic Commission for Latin America in Santiago, Chile. Birns also taught and lectured for 15 years in the fields of Latin American studies, comparative government, and international law at a number of U.S. and British colleges and universities.

Heinz Oberlander.bio: Peter Oberlander (1922-2008) was a Canadian architect and Canada’s first professor of urban and regional planning. He obtained his Bachelor of Architecture degree from McGill University and his Master of Urban Planning and Ph.D. in Urban and Regional Planning from Harvard University. At Harvard, Walter Gropius suggested that Oberlander and fellow student Harry Seidler enroll for the 1946 Summer Art Institute at Black Mountain College to study with Josef Albers. At the University of British Columbia, Oberlander established Canada’s first department of Urban and Regional Planning. In Ottawa, he initiated the federal government’s Ministry of Urban Affairs. With his support and encouragement, the United Nations World Urban Forum III was held in Vancouver in 2006. Posthumously, he was awarded the United Nations Scroll of Honour Award on World Habitat Day, October 4, 2009.

Charlotte Schlesinger.bio: Charlotte Schlesinger was a German pianist and composer. She was a student of Franz Schreker at the Berlin Hochschule für Musik from 1925-1930. In 1935 she left the Vienna Conservatory to teach at the Ukrainian S.S.S.R. Conservatory. Schlesinger migrated to America as a refugee in 1938.

Stephen Forbes.bio: Stephen was a student from fall 1935 to spring 1942 and focused on physics. Before BMC, he attended Milton Academy 1923-1930 and Harvard College 1930-1934, and Harvard summer school 1932 and 1933. He shared in his application, "In 1932-1934 Harvard took up so much of my time I had very little left over for other things. In 1934-1935 I was sick the whole winter so I could do nothing that year. However, I used to have a great interest in numbers (progressions, factors, etc.). Also I was very much interested in the populations of cities, particularly those in the United States.”

Ernst Bacon.bio: Ernst Bacon was an acclaimed American composer, pianist, and conductor. Born in Chicago, Bacon attended Northwestern University, the University of Chicago, and the University of California, Berkeley. Although mostly self-taught as a composer, he studied briefly with Karl Weigl in Vienna, Austria. He was on the faculty of the Eastman School of Music and the San Francisco Conservatory of Music and was appointed to head the WPA Music Project in San Francisco. He also founded the Carmel Bach Festival. His chief teaching positions were at Converse College in Spartanburg, SC (1938-45) and Syracuse University (1945-64), where he retired as Professor Emeritus.

Heinrich Jalowetz.bio: Heinrich Jalowetz was an Austrian musicologist and conductor. He was one of the core members of what became known as the Second Viennese School in the orbit of Arnold Schoenberg. He was music faculty at BMC from fall 1939 to about January of 1946 shortly before his passing.

Joan Baim.bio: Joan attended Black Mountain for one semester in the spring of 1950 and studied Social Science with Levi, Ethics with Dehn, Dancing with Jennerjahn, Writing wtih Richards, and she participated in the Community Work Program. She was noted to have worked at Camp Tamiment in the Pocono Mountains of Pike County, Pennsylvania, as a youth counselor in 1953.

She got permission to attend for a partial semester in the summer. While a student, she participated in Dime a Dance, by Merce Cunningham. She was a member of the Cunningham Dance Company in 1953.

Helen Lounsbury.bio: Helen was listed in college documents as a "hostess," but she also assisted regularly in the theater department. She's noted as helping to create costumes and wigs for theater productions until her resignation in 1944.

Sandra Kocher.bio: Sandra Kocher is the daughter of Margaret and A. Lawrence Kocher, who taught architecture at Black Mountain College from the fall of 1940 through the 1943 summer session. She was almost seven when she arrived at Black Mountain. While at Black Mountain College, Kocher designed the Studies Building, a barn, music practice cubicles, and two small houses, one for the music teacher and his wife, and one for the kitchen staff and other black workers.

Alfred Einstein.bio: Alfred Einstein was a German-American musicologist and music editor. He is best known for being the editor of the first major revision of the Köchel catalogue, which was published in the year 1936.

Paula Lenchner.bio: P‍aula was a student in music with a focus on vocals, for the summer and fall of 1944. She also performed at Bayreuth for 3 seasons, appearing in smaller roles: Wellgunde, Gerhilde, Flowermaiden, Knappe. Other companies she performed with in Germany were Stadttheater von Breman, Stuttgart State Opera and Stadttheater von Mainz.

Her teacher Hale Woodruff told her about a scholarship being offered by the Rosenwald Fund for study at the 1946 Summer Art Institute at Black Mountain. The college had enrolled its first black students in the summer of 1944, and Washington remembered that althoughthe South was still segregated, she felt comfortable attending.

Andrew \"Jack\" Lipsey.bio: Jack and Rubye Lipsey were both cooks at the Blue Ridge Assembly and joined Black Mountain College when the lease transferred to the College. Jack was born Andrew Winston Lipsey, in Union County, South Carolina, May 19, 1888.

Marcia Chamberlain.bio: Marcia Russell Chamberlain was born in San Diego, California April 13, 1926 to structural steel engineer Marshall B. Chamberlain and Dorothy Taylor Chamberlain. Chamberlain attended H. Hoover High School from 1941 to 1944 and earned her diploma. From 1944 to 1949 she attended San Diego State College (B.A.). She then enrolled at the University of Southern California from 1944 to 1946 and at San Francisco State College again from 1949 to 1950 without earning another degree.

Gwendolyn Knight Lawrence.bio: Painter Gwendolyn Knight first came to the United States from Barbados when she was seven years old. At the age of 13, she moved with her family from Saint Louis to Harlem, in the midst of the Harlem Renaissance.

Ralph Lounsbury.bio: Ralph Lounsbury was founding faculty in fall of 1933, teaching government and law. He passed away during the first semester from a paralytic stroke.

Albert \"Bill\" Levi.bio: Bill Levi was faculty of social science and philosophy from fall 1945 to fall 1950. He received an AB in sociology from Dartmouth College in 1932 and an AM and PhD from the University of Chicago. After leaving BMC, he taught at Washington University in St. Louis until his retirement. He is author of a number of books including Philosophy and the Modern World, Philosophy as Social Expression, Literature, Philosophy and the Imagination, and many others.

He had examiners from Harvard and George Washington University that felt he didn't have a full grasp on the history of english literature. Many notes share that he wouldn't have made a good writer and wasn't a promising student.

He obtained what he says is the same as a MA in Agricultural Engineering.

Paul Radin.bio: Paul Radin was a cultural anthropologist and folklorist of the early twentieth century specializing in Native American languages and cultures.

Marje Pearman.bio: Marje Pearman was a secretary for the summer of 1949. She had a background in secretarial work at Donnelly Garment Company and she worked as a personal shopper and "fashion counselor" at Ashell's.

Fernando \"Paco\" Leon.bio: Fernando Leon (1919-2009) was an engineer. Before immigrating to the United States, he and his brother Francisco “Paco” Leon fought with the resistance in Spain in the Spanish Civil War. Francisco, who died from tuberculosis which he contracted in the war, also enrolled at Black Mountain College (BMC). Leon received his B.S. in engineering from Columbia University and his Master of Automotive Engineering from the Chrysler Institute. He worked at Chrysler on development of the XIV-2220 aircraft engine and was a founder of FOREL Equipment Co. in New York City, an exporter of steelmaking and metalworking equipment which helped set up industrial plants in Latin America and Europe under the Marshall Plan. Later he founded Om-El Corporation in Bay City, Michigan, with similar activities as FOREL. Leon was a trustee for Marlboro College in Vermont where Roland Boyden, a former BMC teacher, served in many roles. Leon was married to BMC student Eleanor “Elie” Smith Leon.

Leonard \"Knute\" Stiles.bio: Knute Stiles (1923-2009) was a painter, collagist, art critic, and writer. During World War II, he served in Alaska and thereafter spent summers working on salmon boats and organizing workers. He enrolled at Black Mountain College in 1946 and studied with Ilya Bolotowsky. In San Francisco, he was briefly co-owner with Leo Krikorian of The Place, an influential bar in San Francisco’s North Beach district that was a gathering place for Beat writers and artists. Stiles taught drawing at the San Francisco Art Institute and wrote criticism for Art Forum and Art in America. He was a founder and member of San Francisco’s East-West House, a communal living space, where many artists and writers lived.

Claude Monteux.bio: Claude Monteux was a flutist and composer. He attended BMC from 1937 to 1939.

John Hamilton.bio: John William Hamilton III was a student for the 1951-52 and 1952-53 regular sessions and for the 1952 summer session. John was an undergraduate student at the University of North Carolina in mathematics and art before coming to BMC. He also was active in the veterans’s association.

Alan Hamilton.bio: Graham Hamilton was a student for the summer of 1948. Graham and Jim Leven came to BMC to study architecture with Edgar Kaufmann.

Emelyn Rogers.bio: Emelyn Rogers was a student in the summer of 1949 where she took Weaving with Marli Ehrmann.

Alex Kemeny.bio: Alex Kemeny was a student in the summer of 1951. While at the college, he contributed to the Black Mountain College Review, published in June of 1951. He is listed as an editor and contributed a poem titled

Betsy Weinrib.bio: Betsy Weinrib was a student in the summer of 1953 where she took Weaving with Marie Murelius.

Marion Mitchell.bio: Marion Mitchell was a student for the 1936-1937 school year.

Margaret Williamson.bio: Margaret Williamson Peterson was a student at Black Mountain College in the summer of 1945. At the time she was a third-year pre-med student at McGill University in Canada. She had previously taken art lessons at the Montreal Art Gallery with Goodridge Roberts and Arthur Lismer, the latter one of Canada’s “Group of Seven” painters.

Mignon Couser.bio: Mignon Couser was guest faculty in English and Writing in the summer of 1943.

Ruth Herschberger.bio: Ruth was a student from 1938 to 1939. Before coming to BMC, she attended the University of Chicago, 1935-1937. She was a poet and used the pen name Josephine Langstaff. She published two books of poems,

Joanna Graudan.bio: Joanna Graudan was guest faculty of music in the summer of 1944.

Thomas \"Tommy\" Cutshaw.bio: Thomas was a student from winter 1945 to spring 1946. He focused on piano and worked extensively with Lowinsky.

Judith \"Judy\" Mandelbaum.bio: Judy Mandelbaum was a student from fall 1943 to summer 1944. While a student, she participated on the membership committee.

Mark Schindler.bio: Mark Schindler was a student at Black Mountain College from 1940 to 1942 studying physics and mathematics with Peter Bergmann and Nathan Rosen. He graduated from Reed College and earned a master’s degree in physics from the University of Southern California.

James Bishop.bio: James Bishop was a student for the summer session of 1953. He took Drawing and Painting with Estaban Vicente. When he applied, he stated that he was a student in the Fine Arts at Washington University and wanted to take summer coursework. He also attended Syracuse University.

Robert Haas.bio: Robert Haas was a Viennese photographer, calligrapher, and printer who was a resident photographer from April 17 to June 10 in 1940. He taught students photography and made a photographic study of the college. He later went on to establish The Ram Press in New York.

Dorothy Mayhew.bio: Dorothy Mayhew was a student in fall of 1946.

Frank Eugene Nacke.bio: Frank Nacke followed his older sister Marian Nacke Teeter to Black Mountain College in the fall of 1938.

Barbara \"Andy\" Anderson.bio: Barbara Anne "Andy" Anderson was a student of the college for one semester. While a student, she was involved with the Membership Committee. She returned in 1943 to assist with the building project.

Page \"P.B\" Blakemore.bio: Page Blakemore was a student for the fall of 1936.

Harold Schuyler.bio: Harold Schuyler was a student for the 1944-1945 school year.

Elizabeth Hillard.bio: Elizabeth Hillard was a student from 1935 to 1936. She married John Arthur Harrington, May 27, 1939

George Alsberg.bio: George Meinhard Alsberg was a student at the college from the fall of 1934 to the spring of 1937. He took coursework ranging from music, to history, to economics. No college bulletins share any of George's activities while at the college, but an obituary was posted in 2020 that shares more about his life after attending BMC.

Vernon Phillips.bio: Vernon Phillips was a student from fall 1948 to spring 1950. Before BMC she attended Colorado Springs Fine Arts Center, June 1948 (Principal/ Headmaster was Jean Charlot, who submitted a reference letter for Vernon).

Gertrud \"Trude\" Guermonprez.bio: Trude Jalowetz Guermonprez was born in Danzig, Germany and attended the School of Fine and Applied Arts in Halle-Saale, where she studied weaving under the Bauhaus-trained artist Benita Otte. In 1933, she earned a professional diploma from the Textile Engineering School in Berlin and received a fellowship to study Scandinavian weaving in Sweden and Finland. Upon completion of her studies, Guermonprez moved to Holland where she continued to foster her understanding of technical weave structures and patterns, working for the Dutch hand weaving production studio Het Paapje.

Miriam \"Mim\" Sihvonen.bio: Of the four Sihvonen children, three attended Black Mountain College. Miriam "Mim" Sihvonen was the oldest and the second to enroll from 1947 to 1949.

Cicely Shellhase.bio: Cicely Shellhase was a student in 1950.

Trueman MacHenry.bio: Trueman MacHenry was a student from fall of 1949 to spring of 1952

Herbert Herb Cable.bio: Herb Cable was a student from fall of 1946 to 1948. As he grew up in Los Angeles, many of his references were from creatives around the LA area, including a producer from Paramount Pictures. Not much is shared about his time as a student, but he was listed as Fire Chief.

Kendall Durant.bio: Kendall Durant was a student from 1947 to 1948.

Elizabeth Baker.bio: Elizabeth Baker worked as office staff for the fall semester of 1954. She was also editor for North Carolina Historical Review.

Benjamin \"Ben\" Sneed.bio: Ben Sneed was staff at the college from 1945 to 1953. He worked in maintenance, construction, and in the kitchen.

Mary Leo.bio: Mary Leo was a student from 1946 to 1947. While a student, she participated in a spring concert in March 1946, noted "A Cycle of three songs with words by

Suzanne \"Suzi\" Gablik.bio: Suzi Gablik was a student in the summer of 1951. She was a well-known artist, author, art critic, and professor of art history and art criticism.

Delores Fullman.bio: Delores Fullman joined the college student body in the spring of 1947, which was the first semester after the interracial program deemed the college desegregated. She was the only student in this group of five black students to stay beyond the first semester.

Denise Martin.bio: Denise Martin was a student in 1945. She participated in women's chorus and played the flute at student concerts.

Virginia Seay.bio: Virginia Seay was a student for the 1944 Summer Music Institute. She graduated from Vassar College in 1944 with a degree in Music Composition before BMC, studying under composer and music scholar Ernst Krenek. After BMC, she earned a master's degree from Hamline University in Saint Paul, Minnesota

Marie Murelius.bio: Marie Murelius was an instructor of weaving from 1947 to 1952.

Egbert \"E.W.\" Swackhamer.bio: Egbert Swackhamer was a television and film director. He was a very active student at the college from 1943 to 1948.

Willie Gardner.bio: Willie Gardner was kitchen staff for at least the 1944 school year.

Mendez Marks, Jr..bio: Mendez Marks was a drama student at the college from at least 1940 to 1942.

Emma Mora.bio: Emma Mora was a student for the 1947-1948 school year.

Charles Lindsley.bio: Charles Halsey Lindsley was faculty of chemistry from 1938 to 1941. After leaving BMC, Lindsley worked at the "University of Virginia where he is doing special work for the United States government," according to a January 1944 bulletin. He later worked at America Enka Co. in Asheville, NC. He passed in 1971 from a hiking fall, which was reported by the

Sheila Oline.bio: Sheila Oline was a student from 1946 to 1948.

Johanna Jalowetz.bio: Johanna Jalowetz was faculty of art from fall of 1949 to spring 1953. She taught bookbinding and voice classes.

Felix Wassermann.bio: Felix Wassermann was a German-Jew refugee and guest lecturer for the Seminar on America which was held in the summer of 1943.

Ruth Goldenberg.bio: Ruth was a student in summer of 1948.

Elsa Kahl.bio: Elsa Kahl Cohen was faculty from fall 1942 to summer 1944. College bulletins shared her arrival with "ELSA KAHL, leading director of the Ballet Jooss, came to teach “eukinetics”- a study of motion -when ballet disbanded last year."

Laura Fisher.bio: Laura Fisher was a student from 1933 to 1934. She was part of the founding Rollins students that came up from Florida with the faculty to start BMC. She took a weaving class with Anni Albers in the spring of 1934.

Garland \"Gary\" Clements.bio: Garland was a student at the University of Chicago before coming to BMC. He attended the winter semester of 1945 and left to serve in the Army. He returned for the fall semester of 1947.

Dorothy Noyes.bio: Dorothy Noyes was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

Alain \"Winnie\" Windholz.bio: Alain Windhoiz was a student at the college from 1939 to 1941. He took Weaving 1 with Anni Albers in Fall 1939, but was marked as "dropped."

Harold Raymond.bio: Unable to attend the last two years of high school because of illness, Harold Raymond was tutored privately at his home in Melrose, Massachusetts. Having experienced an unconventional high school education, he was concerned that he might not be comfortable in a conventional college setting. A cousin who was teaching in New York City recommended Black Mountain College to him.

Arlyn McKenna.bio: Arlyn McKenna was a student for the 1943-1944 school year. While a student, she was also secretary to registrar.

George Beiswanger.bio: The Beiswangers come to the college in the summer of 1944 to teach dance.

William \"Bill\" Hanchett, Jr..bio: William was a student from fall 1941 to spring 1942.

Marian Nacke.bio: In Denver, Colorado, Marian Nacke Teeter read the Reader’s Digest condensed version of Louis Adamic’s article about Black Mountain College. She recalled that her family had a "radical viewpoint politically" – they were socialists – and she was not interested in traditional schools.

Wesley \"Wes\" Huss.bio: Wes Huss wore many hats at the college, from fall of 1950 to it's closing in 1956, including theater director and faculty, treasurer, and business manager.

Henry Leonard.bio: Henry Leonard was a guest for the Seminar on America in 1943.

Doris Bollen.bio: Doris Bollen was a student for the fall and winter of 1944. She worked as a stenographer and typist before coming the BMC and while at the college, she worked as the secretary to the rector. She participated in the play,

Gerda Slavson.bio: Gerda Slavson was a student at the college for fall 1948.

Adele Millhendler.bio: Adele Millhendler was a student in 1948.

Mary Ferris.bio: Mary was a student for spring of 1938.

Maxine Haleff.bio: Maxine was a student for the summer of 1949.

Barbara Hoyt.bio: Barbara Hoyt was a student from 1934 to 1936.

Warren \"Pete\" Jennerjahn.bio: Warren P. “Pete” Jennerjahn enrolled at Black Mountain College in the summer of 1948 with his wife Betty, a former student. He had completed his M.S. degree in art at the University of Wisconsin, Madison. At Black Mountain in the fall he was both student and assistant to Josef Albers. In the spring and summer of 1949 he was instructor in art.

Patricia Passlof.bio: Patricia Passlof was a student for the 1948 Summer Art Institute. After BMC, she got her BA from Cranbrook Academy of Art and was a well-known abstract expressionist painter. She studied with Willem de Kooning at the college and continued to work with him after leaving. She was married to artist Milton Resnick and was active in The Club in New Yotk.

Sue Spayth.bio: Having attended a progressive elementary school in New Jersey, Sue Spayth Riley was eager to find a college with a similar philosophy. After reading Louis Adamic’s article "Education on a Mountain" in the April 1936 issue of Harper’s, she applied to Black Mountain College.

Yella Pessl.bio: Yella Pessl was a harpsichordist, pianist and organist. She was a visiting performer in the summer of 1944. She studied at the State Academy of Music in Vienna.

Charles Freeman.bio: Charles Freeman was a student at the college from fall 1939 to spring 1940. After leaving the college he lived in New York (noted around 1967). He was a radio program director by 1950.

William Rice.bio: William Rice was a student from fall 1946 to spring 1939. Before BMC, he attended Classical High School 1931-1936.

Galway Kinnell.bio: Galway Kinnell was a student in summer of 1947.

Avis Belt.bio: Avis studied at the college from 1938 to 1941. Before coming to BMC, she studied music at the Peabody Conservatory of Music in Baltimore.

Gertrud Wenzel.bio: Gertrud was a student from fall 1951 to spring 1952. Before BMC she attended Shanghai British School in Shanghai, China 1946-1948 and Buxtom School, Williamston, Massachusetts 1949-1951.

Doris Miller.bio: Doris came to Black Mountain for the summer session of 1947 to study voice and piano. She and her husband lived in Asheville, so they did not stay on campus during the session, nor did they intend to stay beyond the summer session. She also noted in her application that she knew Carol Brice, who performed at the college during a music institute summer.

John Campbell.bio: John Campbell was a student from fall 1940 to at least spring of 1941.

Evelyn Williams.bio: Evelyn Williams was a student at the college in the summer of 1946. She took Weaving with Anni Albers, but was marked as "dropped."

Margot Kugelman.bio: Margot Kugelman was a student of art in the summer of 1945. She withdrew before the semester ended.

Sara \"Selly\" Sylvester.bio: Sara "Sally" Sylvester was a student at the college from the founding semester in 1933 to 1936. She took Weaving with Anni Albers in 1934 and 1935 and participated in the college's farm program.

Louis Selders.bio: Louis Selders attended Black Mountain for the spring of 1947 as a transfer student from LeMoyne College, and he intended to return to LeMoyne after the spring. He shared in his application to Black Mountain that he was the Student Director of Drama at LeMoyne, “which entitled making scenery, costumes and other things necessary for play production.” He also stated that he was interested in the relationships between minority groups of Jews and Negroes and aimed to learn from attending “the true meaning of the brotherhood of man.”

William \"Willie\" Joseph.bio: William Joseph was a student from 1941 to 1951. He served in Army Air Force during WWII. Before BMC, he attended Attended University School of Cincinnati ,1924-1936, Dartmouth College 1936-1937, Attended Harvard University- College, 1937-1940- B.A., and Harvard University Graduate School of Design, 1940-1941.

Don Warrington.bio: Don Warrington served as the Treasurer for the college for the fall of 1949 and the 1950-1951 school year.

Laura Fischer.bio: Laura was a student from the fall of 1933 to spring of 1934.

Roberta Blair.bio: Roberta Jean Blair was an artist and art educator. Blair taught at Art for the Vineland and Cape May Public Schools in New Jersey. She was a student at the college from the summer of 1944 for the Summer Art Institute and stayed on for the following fall to study photography.

Nellore \"Alice\" Swan.bio: Alice Swan was a student from the founding semester in 1933 to 1935. She took Weaving with Anni Albers in the winter of 1934.

Josephine \"Maria\" Hansgirg.bio: Maria Hansgirg was faculty of French from fall 1942 to summer 1947.

Olivia Silberberg.bio: Olivia Silberberg Toubman (1921-2020) was cellist with the Oklahoma Symphony Orchestra when she was invited to perform at the 1949 summer session at BMC. Silberberg received her soloist diploma from the Longy School of Music in Cambridge, Massachusetts in 1942. The four Silberberg sisters formed the Silberberg String Quartette, which performed in the Boston and Worcester area. She was a member of the Boston Pops Orchestra, the Oklahoma Symphony, and the Atlanta Symphony, as well as chamber groups.

Concetta Scaravaglione.bio: Concetta Scaravaglione was guest faculty of sculpture at the 1946 Summer Art Institute. Scaravaglione had a long career a sculptor and teacher. While she worked in wood, stone, bronze, and copper, her preferred media was terra-cotta. As her work evolved, it became more abstract.

Jane Bartoli.bio: Jane Bartoli was a pianist and gave lecture recitals on the development of the piano-violin sonata and lead string ensembles in the summer of 1947. She studied at University of Pittsburgh. She was a concert pianist, having played in Carnegie Hall. She married Lino Bartoli, a Pittsburgh Symphony violinist and moved to Texas when Lino accepted Baylor University professorship.

Peter \"Pete\" Heinemann.bio: Peter was a student at the college from 1948 to 1949. Before BMC, he attended Windsor Mountain School. After college, he taught painting at the School for the Visual Arts in New York.

Howard \"Rondy\" Rondthaler.bio: Howard Rondthaler was a student from 1952 to 1955 and family to faculty members. He graduated with a concentration of writing and literature with examiner, Robert Creeley.

Eleanore Bermann.bio: Eleanore Bermann was born in New York, New York. She was only sixteen when she enrolled at Black Mountain College for the 1945 Summer Art Institute where she studied with Josef Albers, Lyonel Feininger, Fannie Hillsmith, Robert Motherwell, and Ossip Zadkine.

Irene Simon.bio: Irene Simon was a student for the 1944 Summer Art institute.

Ralph Beckley.bio: Ralph wrote to the college for nearly three years asking for financial aid so he could attend. It wasn't until December of 1937 that his aid request was granted. He took coursework in literature and applied for senior examinations multiple times and was not admitted. After his third attempt, he left the college.

Nikolai Graudan.bio: Nikolai Graudan was a cellist and guest faculty of music for the summer of 1944.

Morris \"Mouse\" Simon.bio: Morris “Mouse” Simon was a student at Black Mountain College from 1940-1941. He grew up in Union City, New Jersey where his father had a haberdashery. He took a general curriculum including mathematics, political theory, drama, literature and art.

Edwin \"Eddie\" Woldin.bio: Judd Woldin grew up in Somerville, New Jersey, where his father worked in the family shoe store. In the fall of 1944, he enrolled at Black Mountain College to study with the composer Heinrich Jalowetz. He completed that year at the college and enrolled for the 1945-46 fall and winter quarters.

Syril Bright.bio: Sybil Bright was a student for the summer of 1953. She was interested in studying with Wesley Huss. After attending BMC, she was a secretary for Temple University.

Leo Lionni.bio: Leo Lionni, a painter, sculptor, graphic designer, educator, and writer and illustrator of children’s books, was a member of the summer arts faculty at Black Mountain College in 1946. Lionni was born in Amsterdam, Holland in 1910 to an Italian family.

René Pinchuk.bio: René Pinchuk was a student for the summer of 1946. He graduated from Cass Technical High School in Detroit and friend and fellow BMC student, Ray Johnson recommended he come to BMC. After leaving, he attended Wayne State University and received a degree in design.

Homer Boblin.bio: Homer was a student for the fall of 1942. He shared in his application that he was interested in gaining "a thorough business education and a broad cultural backgorund." He had just graduated high school when applying and all of his reference mention that he is shy and timid, but a good student.

Eduard Steuermann.bio: Eduard Steuermann was guest faculty of music in the summer of 1944. Steuermann studied piano with Vilém Kurz at the Lemberg Conservatory and Ferruccio Busoni in Berlin, and studied composition with Engelbert Humperdinck and Arnold Schoenberg.

William Hinckley.bio: William Hinckley was founding faculty in psychology that came from Rollins College. He received his BA from Rollins College in 1931 and taught at BMC from fall 1933 to fall 1934.

Peter Nemenyi.bio: Peter Nemenyi was a student from summer 1947 to spring 1950. He became a well known mathematician working in statistics and probability theory, and also an activist.

Wilfrid \"Will\" Hamlin.bio: Will Hamlin was a student at the college from 1940 to 1942. He also served as Guest Faculty, worked in the Print Shop, was active in the work camp, and participated in the College Publicity Bureau.

Nataraj Vashi.bio: Nataraj Vashi was guest faculty in dance and Hindu philosophy for the Summer Art Institute of 1949.

Elaine Bonaparte.bio: Elaine Bonaparte attended the 1945 Summer Music Institute.

Norma Cormany.bio: Norma Cormany was a student at the college from 1944 to 1945. Her advisor was Anni Albers and she was part of the Chemical Crew.

Dorothy Cole.bio: Dorothy was a student from the fall of 1945 to the spring of 1947. While a student, she participated in student concerts and worked in the music library. She took a range of coursework in the arts, music, and social sciences. All of her faculty notes were very positive, across all subjects, and Josef Albers was especially impressed in her work. After her time at BMC, she went on to do illustrations and textile design.

Walter \"WC\" Barnes.bio: Walter C. Barnes was an educator in the fields of Modern European History, English History, Russian, China, and Japan. Barnes regularly published on topics related to Soviet Russia, and historical topics for Events and the Journal of Modern History. He taught History at the college from the fall of 1938 to the spring of 1941.

Roger Sessions.bio: Roger Sessions was guest faculty of music in the summer of 1944. Sessions was an American composer, teacher, and writer on music. He had initially started his career writing in a neoclassical style, but gradually moved further towards more complex harmonies and postromanticism, and finally the twelve-tone serialism of the Second Viennese School.

Theodoros Stamos.bio: Theodoros Stamos was guest faculty of painting and drawing in 1950.

Francis \"Faf\" Foster.bio: Francis Arthur Foster attended the college from the winter of 1941 to the summer of 1948. He left the college around 1945 to serve in the Army and work with the Red Cross and then returned to graduate after his service.

Dorothy Carr.bio: Dorothy Carr was a student from fall of 1944 to spring of 1946. She took Introductory Weaving with Anni Albers (and student teacher Marilyn Bauer) in the fall of 1944.Within that time she took a leave of absence for at least the fall semester of 1945. While a student, she was part of the ladder crew, fire committee, and regularly played the viola for the student body.

Karl Niebyl.bio: Karl Niebyl taught economics from spring 1946 to summer 1951. Niebyl came to the United States in 1934, after escaping from Nazi Germany.

Rudolf Kolisch.bio: Rudolf Kolisch was a Viennese violinist and leader of string quartets, including the Kolisch Quartet and the Pro Arte Quartet. He was guest faculty of music for the Summer Music Institute of 1944.

Alice Rondthaler.bio: Alice Rondthaler (1945-1948) was a typing and shorthand tutor from the 1945 summer session to the 1948 summer session.

Henry Black.bio: Henry Black was a student at the college for the summer of 1943. He immigrated from Germany and his original name was Heinz Schwarzchild.

Eva Heinetz.bio: Eva Heinitz was a German musician, best known as a cellist but also highly acclaimed for her recordings on the viola da gamba. She was a guest faculty in music at the Summer Music Institute of 1945.

Sydney Irwin.bio: Sydney Irwin was a student at the college.

John Corrington.bio: John Corrington was a student at the college from 1945 to 1946. He is mentioned in college bulletins doing public play readings for the student body.

Stuart \"Squeaky\" Atkinson.bio: Stuart Atkinson was a student at the college from the spring of 1945 to the spring of 1947. While a student, he was involved in the French Club and served as the Fire Chief. Students and faculty referred to Stuart as "Squeaky."

Maryrose Margaretten.bio: Maryrose Margaretten was a student from 1947 to 1948.

Theodore \"Ted\" Dreier.bio: Theodore “Ted” Dreier was the son of a prominent family of idealists committed to the arts, social action, women’s rights, and poverty programs. Ted studied electrical engineering at Harvard University from 1920-1925 then worked at General Electric until 1930. A friend, John Malcolm Forbes, brought Dreier to Rollins College where he taught until 1933. Along with the group of staff that left Rollins with John Andrew Rice, he then joined the founding faculty of Black Mountain College in the summer of 1933.

Elizabeth \"Betty\" Mosley.bio: Elizabeth Mosely was secretary at the college for the 1941-1942 school year.

Louise Hetherington.bio: Louise Hetherington was faculty of music from fall 1949 to fall 1951.

Elaine Schmitt.bio: As a child Elaine Schmitt (Urbain), who was born in 1925 in Wauwatosa, Wisconsin, was frequently at Conrad Schmitt Stained Glass Studios, founded by her grandfather in 1885 in Milwaukee. Urbain, along with her siblings, helped in the Studios and was exposed to art at an early age.

Elizabeth Estill.bio: Elizabeth was a librarian at the college and attended a two-week ceramics course in the summer of 1954.

Peggy Bennett.bio: Peggy Bennett was a student at the college from the fall of 1944 to the spring of 1945. She was very interested in writing and studying in a place that would allow her to be introduced to knew things, so she could write about the experiences.

Dorothy Darrell.bio: Dorothy Darrell was a student in the summer and fall of 1953.

Jsrael \"J.B.\" Neumann.bio: J.B. Neumann taught art appreciation in the 1944 Summer Art Institute. J.B. was a gallery director, art dealer and publisher. After immigrating to the U.S., Neumann founded the New Art Circle Gallery in New York City. Before then, he had art galleries in Berlin, Munich, Dusseldorf and Bremen, Germany.

Ronald Robertson.bio: Ronald Robertson enrolled at Black Mountain College for the1951 summer and fall terms. There he studied painting and drawing with Ben Shahn and Robert Motherwell.

Dorothy Breeskin.bio: Dorothy Breeskin attended the 1944 Music Institute, along with her mother (Adelyn Dohme Breeskin) and two sisters. She participated in the New England Conservatory of Music, and is noted as cellist and acapella singer.

Lorraine Creesy.bio: Lorraine was a student from spring 1938 to spring 1940. Lorraine married Leon Wilbur Miller.

Robert Babcock.bio: Robert Babcock was an educator and politician, that served as a Vermont senate from 1951 to 1955. At Black Mountain College, he taught government and politics from 1940 to 1942. He left in 1942 to work at the United States Department of Treasury as a commercial control specialist. After serving in the Navy during World War II, he returned to teaching at the University of Vermont and obtained his PhD from Northwestern University.

Donald Cooper.bio: Donald Cooper was a student at the college in fall of 1952 to summer 1954.

Monika Lányi-Mann.bio: Monika Lányi-Mann was a student in the fall of 1944. She became a well-known author and feature writer and the the fourth of six children of the Nobel Prize–winning author Thomas Mann.

Helen \"Helsie\" Wright.bio: Helen Wright was a student at the college from 1941 to 1945. She took Introductory to Advanced Weaving with Anni Albers, 1942-1944. She participated in the membership committee, and in many plays,. In 1945 she worked as an office secretary.

Noland took a general curriculum with an emphasis on art, music and ceramics. He left to spend a year in Europe on the GI Bill. After a time in Washington D.C., he moved to New York and studied ceramics at Greenwich House while supporting himself working for newspapers and the Arab Information Center. In ceramics,he explored the fish form as an avenue to abstraction. In Amagansett, he worked in various media, including metal and fiberglass.

Harry Seidler.bio: Harry Seidler was born in Vienna, Austria in 1923. He fled to England as a teenager after the Nazis occupied Austria in 1938. There he studied building and construction at Cambridgeshire Technical School.

Charles Godfrey.bio: Charles Godfrey oversaw construction work at the college between 1940 and 1942.

Nathaniel \"Nat\" Lytle.bio: Nat Lytle was a Black Mountain native (raised in Black Mountain and Asheville) who worked for Black Mountain College for over a decade. In the summers of 1933 and 1934, Nat Lytle worked odd jobs and some cooking at the college. From 1937-1938, he worked as an assistant cook, under Jack and Rubye Lipsey, in the kitchen. After three years in the army, he returned to the college from 1944-1946 and worked in the kitchen and on odd jobs. On Tuesdays, the day off for cooks Cornelia and George Williams, Nat Lytle would help remaining cook Malrey Few with the cooking.

Moreen Maser.bio: Moreen Maser was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

Eva Schlein.bio: Eva Schlein Jungermann, born in Furth (Bavaria) Germany in 1923, was one of a number of refugee students at Black Mountain. She was enrolled at the college for the 1945 spring quarter, the 1945-46 academic year and the 1946 fall session. She also attended the 1945 summer session. Her primary interests were writing, philosophy, psychology, and history. While at BMC, she worked in the library.

James Herlihy.bio: James was a student at the college from fall of 1947 to summer of 1948. In a college bulletin, he was mentioned in another student's updates "James Herlihy is at the Pasadena Playhouse, acting and writing plays."

Robert Hawley.bio: Robert Hawley was a student of English and writing in 1956.

Frank Hursh, Jr..bio: Frank Hursh (b. 1929) is an artist, educator, and animator. Hursh enrolled at Black Mountain College in 1949 to study art. He earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree at the University of Texas at Austin. Hursh used his G.I. Bill benefits after service in the United States Navy to continue his studies in Mexico. Finding his budding career to be more interesting than his academic studies, he pursued his interests as a freelance commercial artistand animator. At Gamma Studios, he was involved in productions, including Rocky and His Friends (Rocky and Bullwinkle). He taught at the Instituto Allende in San Miguel de Allende, Guanajuato. In Querétaro, he created the arts program at the new campus of the Universidad del Valle de México. Hursh’s paintings and drawings are in an Abstract Expressionist style.

Renate Benfey.bio: Renate Benfey Wilkins arrived in the United States with her parents, Eduard and Lotte Benfey, in December 1939. Until Kristallnacht in 1938, her family had not felt threatened by the Nazis. Though Jewish by Hitler’s definition, their faith was Christian. Her father was both a World War I veteran and a judge in Berlin.

Joyce Perry.bio: Joyce Perry was a guest for the work camp in the summer of 1946.

Phyllis Josephs.bio: Phyllis Josephs was a student from fall 1938 to spring 1941, and also attended the 1945 Summer Art Institute. While a student, she served as a student officer.

William \"Rags\" Watkins, III.bio: William Watkins was a student from 1947 to 1948.

Frederick \"Fritz\" Neumann.bio: Frederick Neumann was a Polish-born American musicologist, violinist, conductor and composer. Aside from his music career, he also held a PhD in political science from the University of Berlin. From 1934 to 1937 he served as an export-market analyst in Prague, and ultimately went back to the study of music.

Mercier \"Merce\" Cunningham.bio: Mercier Philip "Merce" Cunningham was an American dancer and choreographer who was at the forefront of American modern dance for more than 50 years. Merce spent three summers at BMC during 1948, 1952, and 1953.

Albert Friscia.bio: Albert was a student in the summer of 1947. He listed Ilya Bolotowsky as a reference on his application and studied sculpture at the college. Before BMC, he attended National Academy of Design 1932-1935 and Art Students League in 1938.

Beatrice Lamb.bio: Beatrice Louise Pitney Lamb was an American editor and writer. She earned a BA from Bryn Mawr College in 1927 and an MA from Columbia University in 1956. She worked with the League of Women Voters in the 1930s, and with the United Nations in the 1940s and published several books on India.

Donald \"Don\" Wight.bio: Donald Wight was a student at the college from 1945 to 1947. His focus was architecture, but he also took Weaving 1 and 2 with Mayer in 1946. While a student, he built looms for the weaving department and worked in the art store.

Josef Breitenbach.bio: Josef Breitenbach was guest faculty in photography for the summer of 1944. Josef was a well-known photographer whose manipulated images and stark photographs were part of the Surrealistic movement.

Mary Callery.bio: Mary Callery taught sculpture at the college at the 1945 Summer Art Institute.

James Adams.bio: James came to BMC as a third year student in the winter of 1956. No transcripts are in his student file, but course cards show his enrollment in general studies.

Wilma Stokely.bio: Wilma Dykeman (1920-2006) was a writer of fiction and non-fiction who chronicled the culture of Appalachia in Western North Carolina. Her three novels are The Tall Woman (1962), The Far Family (1966) and Return of the Innocent Earth (1973). Her non-fiction books include The French Broad (1955), and Prophet of Plenty: the First Ninety Years of Willis Weatherford. In the fall of 1944, at Black Mountain College, she and her husband James Dykeman audited classes taught by Alfred Kazin as well as a class taught by poet George Zabriskie, in the fall of 1944.

Doris Pratt.bio: Doris Pratt worked in the registrar's office in 1946.

Sybil Yamins.bio: Sybil was a student from 1938 to 1940. She participated in Waiting for Lefty in 1940, cast as the secretary. After leaving Black Mountain, she graduated from the School of Business at Simmons College in 1943 and began secretarial work at the Red Cross in New York City. She married Simon Goldberg and devoted her life to raising her children and participating with nonprofit organizations.

Robert \"Bob\" Sunley.bio: Robert “Bob” Sunley was a student at Black Mountain College from 1936 to 1939. He came to the college from Oberlin College. At Black Mountain Sunley took a general curriculum including literature, writing and music. He also took part in drama productions and other activities.

Norman Jamieson.bio: Norman Jamieson was a student in summer to fall of 1942 until he was drafted in November. Before BMC, he attended Amherst.

Thomas \"Tom\" Nee.bio: Thomas “Tom” Nee (1920- 2008) enrolled at Black Mountain College (BMC) to study with composer Stefan Wolpe. Nee was chair of the department of music at the University of California at San Diego where he developed an innovative contemporary music curriculum. He was artistic director and conductor of the La Jolla Symphony for thirty-one years and director of the New Hampshire Music Festival from 1960 until 1992.

Paul Alexander.bio: Paul Alexander (1931-2021) enrolled at Black Mountain College for its last full academic year, 1955-1956. He had to leave before the end of the year when GI Bill benefits were cut. He settled in San Francisco where he was a central figure in the San Francisco Renaissance. He operated Buzz Gallery and held various jobs, including working for Southern Pacific railroad and in the modern art department at Gump’s. He lived in Fort Bragg in MendocinoCounty in the final years of his life.

Thomas Surette.bio: Dr Thomas Whitney Surette was an American composer, musician, and educator. He studied music at Harvard University under John Knowles Paine and Arthur Foole, but did not complete his degree.

Marcel Dick.bio: Marcel Dick was a viola and violin player and had a prominent performing career in Europe with string quartets and orchestras before immigrating to the United States. In Europe, he was a member of the Schoenberg Circle and was invited to perform with Rudolf Kolisch’s summer quartet at Black Mountain College. He was head of the graduate department of theory and composition at the Cleveland Institute of Music and principal violinist with the Cleveland Orchestra.

N.O. \"Pitt\" Pittinger.bio: N.O. Pittinger served as rector at the college in 1949. He was appointed the position for the following school year but declined it, saying the "manner in which the annuities were handled thoroughly disgusts me." (Letter from NO Pittinger to Raymond Trayer, February 21, 1949 in faculty files at Western Regional Archives)

Sarah Towery.bio: Sarah Carlisle Towery was a student at Black Mountain College during the 1944 Summer Art Institute. A painter and teacher, she conducted kindergarten and art classes in her home for fifty years. To celebrate her eightieth birthday, in October 1992, her children organized a gathering of professional friends with whom she had studied and painted over many years. That gathering was the catalyst for the Sarah Carlisle Towery/Alabama Art Colony on Lake Martin in Alexander City.

David Bailey.bio: David studied at Harvard Unversity before coming to Black Mountain. David studied English and focused on Shakespeare in his studies, at both colleges. He failed his senior examinations the first time and took examinations in Shakespeare at Harvard University in 1934. He submit his writtten senior examinations again in 1935 and graduated. In 1936, he worked with Yale University, then with Miquon, a progressive school for small children in Pennsylvania. He returned to Black Mountain from 1938 to 1940 to work as the Publicity Chairman.

Viola Farber.bio: Viola was a dance student from fall 1951 to summer 1953. Viola studied music with Lou Harrison and dance with Katherine Litz. After studying with Merce Cunningham in the summer of 1952, she moved to New York to continue her studies. She returned to BMC the following summer to study with Cunningham and was a founding member of the Merce Cunningham Dance Company. She created many roles for the Cunningham Dance Company and also worked with other choreographers,including Paul Taylor and Katherine Litz. In 1968, she formed The Viola Farber Dance Company.

David Tudor.bio: David Tudor was a guest faculty of Music in the 1951 and 1953 summer sessions. Tudor was a pianist and composer of experimental music.

Russell Edson.bio: Russell was a student in spring of 1951. He left during the semester due to a draft call.

Kenneth Ayres, Jr..bio: Kenneth Richard Ayres was a student at the college from the fall of 1939 to the spring of 1941. Kenneth's student file shows that he was very interested in planes and interested in someday becoming a pilot. He studied mathematics and sciences and seemed to have a rough start at his coursework, but improved as he continued his studies at Black Mountain.

Patricia Nelson.bio: Patricia Nelson Newhall (1933-2016) was a psychiatrist. In New York after leaving Black Mountain College (BMC), she worked at Motorcycles Incorporated, a shop in New York owned by her future husband Daniel Newhall and a place where other BMC students worked. Newhall studied at City College of New York and Temple University. She earned her medical degree from Women’s Medical College of Philadelphia and graduated from the Philadelphia Psychoanalytic Society. She graduated Summa cum Laude at the Tyler Art School of Art and Architecture where she majored in sculpture.

Joan Couch.bio: Joan is known by many names. She attended the college first as Joan Couch. She married fellow student, Oli Sihvonen and became Joan Sihvonen. She later took her mother's maiden name, as Joan Potter. Then married and took the name Joan Potter Loveless.

Eleanor Hawk.bio: Eleanor Hawk was a student for the 1946 Summer Art Institute. Her father was a minister and they lived and travelled around NC. At the college, she took courses with Anni Albers and Jean Varda.

Fritz Moellenhoff.bio: Fritz Moellenhoff (1891-1980) was faculty of psychology from fall 1935 to spring 1939. Prior to coming to the college, Anna and Fritz worked as physicians in Germany.

William Zeuch.bio: William Edward Zeuch was an American socialist, educator, and academic who is best known as a founder and first director of the Commonwealth College in Arkansas. This college is the most well known attempt in Arkansas at establishing a radical labor educational school.

Mary Phelan Outten.bio: Mary Phelan Outten was a student from spring 1945 to summer 1948. She was best known for her landscape paintings.

Jean Brewton.bio: Jean Brewton was a student at Stephen Lee High School, an African-American school in Asheville. Application includes several brochures from the Saint Matthias Church of Asheville. She traveled to BMC for day classes in weaving for the summer of 1955.

Jacqueline Hermann.bio: Jacqueline was a student in the summer of 1950, while still a student at the High School of Music and Art in New York. She studied at the Art Students League and at the Art Institute of Chicago. As a painter, her interest has been in observation and interpretation of landscapes and cityscapes. She groups her paintings in three categories: city paintings, cloud paintings and terrain/in flight paintings.She is a member of the National Academy of Arts and Letters in New York and, in 2004, she was recipient of the Arts and Letters Award.
