Jose Yglesias.bio: Jose was a student in 1946. While a student, he served as a Student Officer as Secretary, on the Discipline Committee, and also participated in a student-run French club. He participated in the Community Council in "preparing a program of community education which will lead to a democratic decision by the community as to how the emergency buildings given to us by the Federal Government are to be utilized," in which he was a secretary.

Raymond \"Ray\" Toubman.bio: Raymond Toubman (1921-2009) was first oboist with the Oklahoma Symphony Orchestra when he was invited to perform at the 1949 summer session at Black Mountain College (BMC). During his career, he was first oboist with the Indianapolis Symphony, the Southern Symphony Orchestra, and the Atlanta Symphony. He performed with the Boston Pops Orchestra under Arthur Fielder and with many Boston organizations. Toubman obtained his master’s degree in library science and his Ph.D. in musicology from Boston University. While working as librarian at the Oglethorpe University Library, Toubman performed as a freelance musician.

Janet \"Aley\" Ramsey.bio: Janet Ramsey was a student from fall 1944 to winter 1946. She shared in her application that she was interested in studying poetry at BMC.

Lana Yarash.bio: Lana was a student from 1943 to 1944. She participated in Betty Kelley’s original three-act fairy play, “More Straw for the Scarecrow,” as Mother Mouse in 1944.

Jeanette \"Jane\" Bland.bio: Jane Bland attended the 1944 Art Institute where she took Textile Design with Anni Albers.

Richard Jordan.bio: Richard Jordan was a student from 1950 to 1951.

Eva Heinitz.bio: Eva Heinitz was a musician, best known as a cellist but also highly acclaimed for her recordings on the viola da gamba. She taught music at the 1945 Summer Music Institute. In 1948, she was appointed to teach at the University of Washington in Seattle.

Paul Bissell.bio: Paul Bissell was a student for the summer 1951 session.

Terence Burns.bio: Terence Burns was a student from the fall of 1952 to winter of 1956. There were some semesters where he only took one course at a time and others where he had a full-time workload. He heard about the college from the Olson Review.

Paula Eicke.bio: Paula Eicke was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

John, who was almost eight when he arrived at Black Mountain, was one of three sons: David Corkran III, John and Robin.

Bela Martin.bio: Bela Martin heard about Black Mountain College at Louisville Male High School from Robert Wunsch, who had taught there between his leaving Rollins College and his teaching at Black Mountain. Martin and Morton Steinau hitchhiked to Black Mountain to visit Wunsch and decided to enroll.

Marie-Louise von Franz.bio: Marie-Louise von Franz was guest faculty in spring of 1953. She was a psychologist and scholar, known for her psychological interpretations of fairy tales and of alchemical manuscripts.

Suzanne Smith.bio: Suzanne Smith was a student for winter 1942 to spring 1943. Before coming to BMC she attended Milton Academy, in Milton, MA from 1935-1938, and Scripps College, 1939-1942. After BMC, she returned to Scripps College to graduate.

Mary Bishop.bio: Mary Alice Bishop was married to Richard “Rich” Bishop (b. June 7, 1928) upon graduation from high school in Elmhurst, Illinois. Immediately thereafter they left for Black Mountain College. She was there intermittently from the summer of 1951 through the summer of 1953. She was a student and then a faculty wife. She studied weaving with Andrew “Andy” Oates. She also studied music and dance.

Mary Fitton.bio: During World War II, Mary Fitton Fiore served in the Women’s Army Corps. She graduated from Radcliffe College in 1946. She enrolled at Black Mountain College in the fall of 1949. After her marriage to Joseph Fiore (February 3, 1925-September 8, 2008), a former student who taught art, she remained at the college as faculty wife until the college closed the Lake Eden campus in September 1956.

Thomas \"Tommy\" Brooks.bio: Thomas Brooks was a student at the college from fall of 1939 to spring of 1942 when he was drafted. He focused on Sociology, with a love for political theory and economics. His application shared that he was interested in teaching and wanted to learn about progressive education methods.

Koon Cheang.bio: Koon Hing Cheang came to the college during the summer of 1942 to participate in the work program.

David \"Dave\" Schauffler.bio: David Schauffler was a student for the 1946-1947 school year. Before BMC, he attended the Putney School in Vermont and afterwards received his master’s degree in music from Northwestern University. He taught music and later worked as a bus driver at the Catlin Gabel School.

Theodore \"Quintus/ Ted\" Dreier, Jr..bio: Theodore “Ted” Dreier, Jr. was born in Albany, New York, near where his father worked for the General Electric Company. He came with his parents to Black Mountain College in the fall of 1933 at its founding. He was four-and-a-half years old.

Jesse Morgan.bio: Jesse Morgan was a student in 1949. While a student he served as a student officer and work coordinator.

Norman West.bio: Norman West was at the college as a student from the founding semester in 1933 to 1939. He studied economics and served in a staff role as the Assistant Treasurer.

Frederick Georgia.bio: Frederick Georgia was founding faculty in fall of 1933 and taught until spring 1937. He came from Rollins college and came to BMC to teach science. He also served as the first rector of the college.

Stefan Wolpe.bio: Stefan Wolpe was a German-born American composer. He was associated with interdisciplinary modernism, with affiliations ranging from the Bauhaus, Berlin agitprop theater and the kibbutz movement to the Eighth Street Artists' Club, Black Mountain College, and the Darmstadt Summer Courses for New Music.

Thomas Raleigh.bio: Thomas Joseph Raleigh was a student in 1945. While a student, he served as a student officer and was part of the hauling crew in the work program.

Alan Lindsay.bio: Alan Lindsay was a student for the summer of 1949.

Franz Kline.bio: Franz Kline was an American painter associated with the Abstract Expressionist movement of the 1940s and 1950s. Kline is best known for his powerful black-and-white abstractions in which the vigorous brushwork seems to embody the energy and gestures created in the act of painting.

Marie Tavroges.bio: Marie Tavroges Stillkind was a student at Black Mountain College in the spring to summer of 1952. A native of Montreal, she had studied art at Sir George Williams College in Montreal, where she met Dorothea Rockburne, a Black Mountain student.

Louis \"Jean\" Charlot.bio: Jean Charlot was guest faculty in art for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

Lenore Gold.bio: Lenore was a student in the summer of 1947. She was a student at the University of Chicago from 1943 to 1945.

Robert Hall.bio: Robert Hall was a student from 1933 to 1937.

George Williams.bio: George Williams was part of the kitchen staff at the college from at least 1944 to 1951.

Ruth Asawa.bio: Ruth Asawa was a student for the 1946 art institute and stayed on as a full-time student until the spring of 1949. While a student, she served as a Student Moderator and on the Board of Fellows. Ruth Asawa was born 1926 in Norwalk, CA. She is known as a sculptor and referred to as the "fountain lady" for her many fountains.

Paul Goodman.bio: Paul Goodman was an American writer and public intellectual best known for his 1960s works of social criticism. Goodman taught poetry in the summer of 1950.

Ada Kopetz.bio: Ada Kopetz was a student for the 1944 Summer Music Institute and stayed on for fall.

Margaret Chandler.bio: Margaret Chandler was admitted as a day student in the fall of 1944 and also attended the 1945 Summer Art Institute. Margaret expressed interest in taking art courses and introductory Spanish and Writing.

Rose Glinsberg.bio: Rose Glinsberg was a student for the 1944 Summer Music Institute.

Donald \"Don\" Calhoun.bio: Donald Calhoun was guest faculty of sociology at the college for the summer of 1948. His courses were on "the Freudians" and "Culture and Personality."

Edward Jenks.bio: Edward Jenks was a student since the founding of the college in fall 1933 until 1935. Before BMC, he attended Harvard 1929-33 and Rollins College in 1933. After he left BMC, he joined the Navy and gave updates for the college bulletin.

Emanuel Zetlin.bio: Emanuel Zetlin taught music at the Summer Music Institute of 1945. While at the college, he shared that he was Associate Concertmaster of the Metropolitan Opera Company and a member of the faculty of the Manhattan School of Music. Zetlin's name can be found in many concert posters and college bulletins for the summer of 1945 for his violin performances.

Boris Aronson.bio: Boris Solomon Aronson was a scenic designer, occasional costume designer, painter and sculptor. He was born around 1900 in Kiev (currently the independent Ukraine), the son of a rabbi, and came of age during the Russian Revolution. He studied art and design at the School of Modern Painting in Moscow, as well as studying with the avant-garde painter and stage designer Alexandra Exter.

Martha Hult.bio: Martha Hult was a student in 1946. Before BMC, she attended Reed College in Portland, OR.

Jeanne Wacker.bio: Jeanne Wacker was a very involved student. She was involved in the International Relations Club which held public debates about current topics. She was also involved in drama productions. She was also involved in student activities on the farm and in the kitchen, helping to organize student duties and responsibilities.

Addison Bray.bio: Addison Bray was a student from the fall of 1943 to summer of 1944. He took Introductory & Elementary Weaving with Anni Albers through the Winter/ Spring semester of 1944. He participated in plays, such as Outward Bound, and The Importance of Being Earnest. He asked for transcripts to be sent to Bard College and Columbia upon leaving BMC. According to Mary Emma Harris' interview with Addison, he taught a general curriculum in New York City high schools, primarily in Harlem.

Leila Bullock.bio: Evelyn Bullock was a student in for the 1949 Summer Art Institute.

Ruthabeth Krueger.bio: Ruthabeth Krueger was a music student from fall 1941 to spring 1942. While a student, she was very active in student concerts and the BMC radio program.

Ray Derbeck.bio: Ray was a student for the summer of 1948.

Sylvia Girsch.bio: Sylvia was a student from fall of 1946 to summer 1948. While a student, she worked on bulletins with M.C. Richards.

Elizabeth \"Lisa\" Jalowetz.bio: Lisa Jalowetz Aronson (1920-2013) was a stage designer and collaborator with Boris Aronson for major Broadway productions including A Little Night Music, Fiddler on the Roof, The Crucible and many others. She worked with notable theater persons including Harry Horner and Norman Bel Geddes. She collaborated with Frank Rich on The Theatre of Boris Aronson, documenting his work as a stage designer. As daughter of conductor Heinrich Jalowetz, she spent her childhood in Austria and Germany. When the Nazis invaded Vienna where she was a student, she escaped to Holland. A student visa from Black Mountain College where her father had been appointed enabled her to immigrate to the United States.

John Bauder.bio: John was a student at the college from the fall of 1952 to the spring of 1953. John applied to Black Mountain for a work scholarship at the age of 36 and hoped to learn more about art and improve his technique.

William Miller.bio: William Blackall Miller (1916-2004) graduated in art history from Harvard University and received his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He taught at the Rhode Island School of Design, Milton Academy, Amherst College, and Colby College. Miller, besides being an artist, was an accomplished calligrapher and a pop craftsman creating limericks, whirligigs, hand bound books, toys and puzzles. He spent a year in Rome on a Fulbright Scholarship and traveled widely. He was active in the Maine League of Historical Societies and Museums and other preservation organizations.

James Prestini.bio: James Prestini was guest faculty of sculpture in the summer of 1944.

Kendall Cox.bio: Kendall Boice Cox was born in Chicago, Illinois to lawyer Arthur Malcolm Cox, Sr. and Mary Edna Boice Cox. He attended North Shore Country Day School from 1930-1943. After graduation, Cox spent two-and-a-half years in the Army.

Stella Balderston.bio: Stella was 47 when she applied for admittance to Black Mountain. She stated in her application that she was hoping to get back into "habits of working out my own ideas" and looking for a "refreshing experience." She shared that she was a Navy Veteran and hoped to help with community life and gardening.

Irene Lott.bio: Irene Lott was a student for fall 1943 and left in January of 1944.

Sylvesta \"Vesta\" Martin.bio: Sylvesta Martin joined the Black Mountain student body for the Summer Music Institute of 1945 and stayed on as the first, full-time black student by the fall of 1945. There isn’t much known about Vesta aside from what can be found from her time at Black Mountain.

Irma Ehrman.bio: Irma Ehrman was a student from winter 1944 to fall 1945. While a student, she participated in student government and worked as a secretary. A bulletin shared "Irma Ehrman has a new job with Alfred H Knopf doing publicity work."

Peter \"Pete\" Hill.bio: Pete Hill was a student from 1940 to 1943, with a leave of absence between while drafted. He attended the Marietta School of Organic Education before BMC. He took his senior examinations then asked for a leave of absence for the duration of the war. He did not return to BMC after the war.

Jene Markoff.bio: Jene Markoff was a student from 1939 to 1946. While a student, Jene regularly wrote for the college bulletins.

Margaret Strauss.bio: Margaret Strauss was a lab assistant for Dr. Fritz Hansgirg in 1944.

Gloria Larsen.bio: Gloria Larsen was a student at the college from 1938 to 1940. She took Introductory Weaving and Advanced Weaving with Anni Albers in 1939 and 1940.

Dorothy Mattison.bio: Dorothy Mattison was active at the college in many ways, from fall of 1942 to summer of 1943. She held an office position as the Publicity Chairperson, she was guest faculty in journalism, and helped coordinate the work camp. She was at the college with her husband and children and continued to write to the bulletin after they left.

Vita Rudikoff.bio: Vita Rudikoff was a student from 1943 to 1944. She was was born in New York in 1925 and lived in Mount Vernon, NY. She attended the New York’s Music & Art High School before BMC. As an adult, she edited a folk songs journal, and ran square dance gatherings during WWII at the USO.

Karen Karnes.bio: Karen Karnes was a ceramist, best known for her salt glazed, earth-toned stoneware ceramics. Karnes was guest faculty and art in residence of ceramics in the summers of 1952 through 1954. She was also a student in the summer of 1946, and "resident production potter."

Harley Parker.bio: Harley Parker was a student in 1946. He graduated from the Ontario College of Art in Toronto, in 1939. He later worked at McLuhan's Centre for Culture and Technology at the University of Toronto as a research associate and instructor of art at the Rochester Institute of Technology.

Lionel Nowak.bio: Lionel Nowak was guest faculty of music in the summer of 1944. He was the Music Director for the Humphrey-Weidman Dance Company (1936-42). From 1948 until 1993 he taught at Bennington College.

Carol Singer.bio: Carol Singer attended in the summer of 1947 with an interest in art and design. When she left after the summer, she asked that her transcripts be sent to Washington Square College of Arts and Sciences, New York.

Jacqueline Singer.bio: Jacqueline Singer Penney, artist, author, teacher and lecturer, was a student at Black Mountain College for the 1949 Summer Institute.

Eleanore \"Elly\" Smith.bio: Eleanore Smith was a student from fall 1944 to . Before BMC, she attended Milton Academy, Milton, Massachusetts, 1940-1943, and the University of Idaho, 1943-1944.

Edward Dahlberg.bio: Edward Dahlberg was an American novelist, essayist, and autobiographer. Dahlberg came to BMC briefly in fall of 1948 to teach writing.

Susan Weil.bio: Weil was a student at Black Mountain College for the 1948–1949 academic year and faculty wife to Robert Rauschenberg in the 1951 summer. At the Académie Julian in Paris in 1948, she met art student Rauschenberg, who subsequently applied to the college. Both studied with Josef Albers, whose exercises in design and color exerted a strong influence.

Hubert \"Bud\" Ray.bio: Ray Hubert was a student from 1949 to 1950 and he took Weaving with Marli Ehrmann in the summer of 1949.

Charles Boyce.bio: Charles Boyce graduated from the University of Indiana just before entering BMC in the fall of 1946. While a student, he was active in the Economics Club, was part of the football team, then known as the Prehistoric Specimen, and participated in an acapella group. He communicated to the college that he was interested in studying economics and left attendance to BMC dependent on their ability to teach the subject. Upon leaving the college, he shared in a college bulletin that he was married to a Barbara Stadthaus and would attend Syracuse University School of City Planning.

Robert Held.bio: Robert was a student from fall 1942 to spring 1943.

John Rice.bio: John Andrew Rice was an educator and founder of Black Mountain College. He was born and raised in South Carolina; his father was a Methodist minister and college educator, and his mother was sister to U.S. Senator, Ellison Durant “Cotton Ed” Smith. Rice attended the Webb School in Tennessee, a college preparatory boarding school, and Tulane University in New Orleans, where he graduated with a bachelors in classics in just three years. Claude Stoller.bio: Claude Stoller was an architect of note, known for his advocacy for social housing and historic preservation. He grew up in the Bronx, New York. Stoller's completion of studies at DeWitt Clinton High School, coincided with the exhibit Bauhaus 1919-1928 at the Museum of Modern Art. Through this exhibition, he became interested in attending Black Mountain College (BMC) in western North Carolina. While at BMC, Stoller took a wide variety of classes, including Josef Albers's courses in design, color, and drawing along with architecture courses led by Lawrence Kocher, Howard Dearstyne, and Lou Bernard Voight. Stoller, along with fellow student Charles Forberg, oversaw the construction of the Jalowetz House, a small dwelling designed by Lawrence Kocher for music instructor Henrich Jalowetz, and his family. BMC also gave Stoller a chance to experiment with photography. In 1942, Claude Stoller was drafted into the United States Army. He served in the 14th Coast Artillery on Puget Sound in Washington State. After attending army engineering school, Stoller served in Germany and France with the 13th Armored Division.

Cynthia Sargent.bio: Cynthia Sargent was a student in fall of 1945 and withdrew in the spring 1946 semester. Before BMC she attended Beaver Country Day School 1937-1940.

Francis Curley.bio: Francis was a student from fall 1946 to spring 1947.

Harriet Florence Sohmers.bio: Harriet Sohmers Zwerling (1928-2019) was a writer, editor, and artist’s model. In Paris in the 1950s, she was associated with the expatriate scene and later part of the literary scene in New York. She was an artist’s model for painters. While a student at Berkeley, she was a friend of Peggy Tolk-Watkins, owner of the Tin Angel, a jazz and crab bar in Sausalito. She obtained her B.A. from Hunter College and, after her marriage to Louis Zwerling,taught elementary school in Brooklyn, New York, for twenty-eight years. She was bisexual and had affairs with Susan Sontag, Irene Fornés and others. Her memoir Notes of a Nude Model and Other Pieces was published in 2003. She appears in the documentary Still Doing It about the sex lives of older women.

George Cadmus, Jr..bio: George Cadmus was a student from fall of 1939 to spring of 1940.

Elizabeth \"Betty\" Brett.bio: Elizabeth Brett was a student from fall of 1939 to summer of 1943.

William McCleery.bio: William McCleery was resident writer for the 1939 spring semester at Black Mountain College. He wrote a play Let Me Have Air which was performed at the college. The songs including “Let Me Have Air,” “I’m 96 a Fool for Freedom,” and others became theme songs which were often performed at college singalongs and other occasions.

Eugene O'Brien.bio: Eugene O'Brien was a guest in 1943 to participate in the work camp.

Jean Maurice.bio: Jean Maurice was a student at the college from 1945 to 1947. Prior to BMC, she attended Smith College, 1943-1945.

Etta Mandelbaum.bio: Etta Deikman notably studied painting with Hans Hoffman at his School of Art in New York City. While at Black Mountain College in the 1948 summer session, she studied painting with Willem de Kooning and sculpture with Peter Grippe. She was there for the legendary summer of John Cage, Merce Cunningham, and Buckminster Fuller who were also brought on by Josef Albers to teach. Deikman approaches each painting as an adventurous journey, finding surprising relationships and ideas as she goes; this sort of freedom of thought and acceptance of chance aligns with the way students were taught at Black Mountain College.

Elizabeth \"Betty\" Spaulding.bio: Elizabeth Spaulding was a founding student, at the college from 1933 to 1936.

Hugh McFadden.bio: Hugh McFadden was a student in fall of 1935.

Doris Johnson.bio: Doris Johnson was a student in the summer of 1946. She also studied at d at George School and John C Campbell Folk School.

Nancy Newhall.bio: Nancy Wynne Newhall was an American photography critic. She is best known for writing the text to accompany photographs by Ansel Adams and Edward Weston, but was also a widely published writer on photography, conservation, and American culture. She was also co-founder of Aperture Magazine.

Barbara Bank.bio: Barbara Bank was a student at the college for the summer of 1944.

Michael Rumaker.bio: Michael Rumaker was a student in writing from fall 1952 to summer 1958. Before BMC he attended Rider College, September 1950- May 1952.

Norman Davis.bio: Norman was a student from spring to summer of 1945.

John \"Danny/ Jack\" Deaver.bio: John “Danny” Virgil Deaver attended BMC from the fall of 1940 until he was drafted in April of 1943. He also participated in the work camp for summer 1941.

Norma Huff.bio: Norma Huff was a dance student in the summer of 1951.

Anthony \"Tony\" Landreau.bio: Anthony “Tony” Landreau taught weaving at Black Mountain College from the fall of 1954 through the 1956 summer session. Born in Washington, D.C. in 1930, he served in the Navy in the Pacific for two years in the late 1940s.

Evelyn Tubbs.bio: Evelyn Tubbs was a student from 1939 to 1941.

Morton \"Mort\" Steinau.bio: Soon after Morton Steinau graduated from Louisville Male High School in Kentucky in January 1935, he and Bela Martin, another graduate, hitchhiked in bitter April weather from Louisville to Black Mountain College where Robert Wunsch was teaching English. They remained for two months.

Thomas Ayres, Jr..bio: Thomas Owen Ayres, Jr. was a student at the college from the fall of 1949 to the spring of 1950. Thomas left during his first semester and was admitted to The Institute for Living in Hartford, CT, for "emotional disturbance characterized by anxiety, disinterest, and withdrawal from social contacts" which also led to his withdraw from the Navy two years prior. After leaving the Institute, he came back to Black Mountain in the spring of 1951, but also left during that semester and did not return.

Gretel Lowinsky.bio: Gretel Lowinsky taught cello, violin, and viola while a faculty member at the college and was also the head Librarian of the Surette Music Library.

Kras Malno.bio: Kras Malno was a guest in 1945 for a concert with the Gordon String Quartet.

Gerald \"Jerry\" van de Wiele.bio: Van de Wiele received his acceptance letter to attend Black Mountain College on the same day he received his draft notice. Following his service in the 2nd Marine Division based out of Camp Lejeune in North Carolina, and further enticed by a letter from his friend Jorge Fick, he decamped to study art and poetry at Black Mountain College in 1954.

Ingeborg \"Inga\" Lauterstein.bio: Ingeborg (Inga) Svar Lauterstein was not only a visual artist, but also a noted author. She won acclaim for her novels which were based on her experiences growing up in Nazi-era Austria. She was a student at the college in 1948.

Seymour Barab.bio: Seymour Barab was a performer and guest lecturer in music for the summer of 1953.

Denis Rhodes.bio: Denis Rhodes was a student from 1936 to 1938. While a student, he participated in student poetry readings, and participated in drama productions,

Edward \"Ed\" Dorn.bio: Edward Dorn was a poet and teacher. Studied at the University of Illinois and at Black Mountain College (1950-1955). At Black Mountain he came into contact with Charles Olson, who greatly influenced his literary worldview and his sense of himself as poet. Dorn's final examiner at Black Mountain was Robert Creeley (q.v.), with whom, along with the poet Robert Duncan, Dorn became included as one of a trio of younger poets later associated with Black Mountain and with Charles Olson. Joined the teaching staff at the University of Essex in 1965. He spent most of the next five years in England, where he published several collections of poems and wrote Book 1 of of his most famous poem 'Gunslinger'

Daniel \"Dan\" Wallace.bio: Dan Wallace was a student for the 1950-1951 school year.

Lydia Griscom.bio: Lydia was a student from fall 1943 to spring 1944. While at the college, she was also a secretary to the treasurer.

Barbara Morgan.bio: Barbara Morgan taught photography at the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

David Tananbaum.bio: David Tananbaum was a student in 1950.

Nancy Smith.bio: Nancy Smith Wright, a native of Wisconsin, enrolled at Black Mountain College for the 1944 Summer Art Institute. She remained for the 1944-45 fall and winter terms and the1945 Summer Art Institute. She was one of a number of students from Milwaukee State Teachers College to attend the college.

Stephen De Staebler.bio: Stephen was a student in the summer of 1951. At time of application, he shared that he exhibited LA and taught at the San Francisco Art Institute.

Joy Ballon.bio: Joy Ballon was a student at Black Mountain College in the summer of 1949. A member of the Anglophone (English speaking) community in Montreal, Quebec, Ballon was an art student at McGill University. Her teacher Arthur Lismer, a member of the “Group of Seven” which were seeking to define a distinctive voice in art for Canada, recommended Black Mountain College to her.

Jacqueline Dunaway.bio: Jacqueline was a student in the summer of 1949.

Lucian Crane.bio: Lucian Crane was a student at the college from fall 1934 to summer 1937.

Nanette \"Nan\" Wright.bio: Nanette Wright was a student for the 1943-1944 school year.

Arthur Adams.bio: Arthur Adams served on the advisory board for the college from 1935 to 1947.

Christian Baensch.bio: Christian's student file shares that he had an interest in the arts and of medical complications that he had. He suffered a birth trauama which left him with paralysis of the right hand and foot and caused periodic blackout episodes. He attended the 1952 Summer Art Institute and created works despite this disability.

Hazel Harris.bio: Hazel Harris was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

Isaac Cramer.bio: Isaac Doughton Cramer was born March 27, 1915 in Camden, New Jersey. He attended the Moorestown Friends’ School in New Jersey from 1929 to 1933. On the recommendation of Frank Aydelotte, President of Swarthmore College and brother-in-law of John Andrew Rice, he enrolled at 40 Black Mountain College in September 1933, making him one of the first students at the new college. He graduated on December 7, 1937.

Mark Hedden.bio: Mark was a student from fall 1948 to spring 1952, attending multiple summer art institutes and graduated with Paul Goodman as his examiner. Before BMC, he attended the Solebury School prep school in Pennsylvania, along with BMC student, Tim LaFarge.

Roberta Fox.bio: Roberta was a student for summer of 1952.

James McClure.bio: James McClure was a student from summer to fall 1947. Before BMC he attended Johns Hill Jr. High School 1941-1942, and Cass Technical High School 1942-1944.

Jack Tworkov.bio: Jack Tworkov was a guest faculty in Painting and Drawing in the 1952 summer session.

Isaac \"Ike\" Nakata.bio: Nisei student Isaac “Ike” Susumi Nakata was born in Hawaii to first-generation immigrants from Japan.

Anna Lenhart.bio: Anna Lenhart accompanied Peter B Lenhart in 1943 while he participated in the work camp. She took classes as a guest.

Gertrud Lukaschik.bio: Gertrud Lukaschik was at the college from October 1938 to February 1939. She was a guest of her brother-in-law, Erwin Straus, while she applied for citizenship from Germany. She returned to Europe in summer of 1939 for "health reasons" according to a letter from Erwin on December 28, 1940.

Kenneth Snelson.bio: Ken Snelson grew up in Pendleton, Oregon where his father John Tavner Snelson had a camera shop. After his discharge from the navy, he enrolled at the University of Oregon in Eugene to study painting. He remembers Jack Wilkinson, the head of the art department, as a man with far-ranging interests and an interesting mind. It was through Wilkinson that he was first introduced to Bauhaus ideas.

Erik Haugaard.bio: Erik was a student from 1941 to 1943. While a student, he contributed to news reports and worked in the summer 1942 work camp. He was drafted while at the college and served as a cadet pilot in the Royal Canadian Air Force.

Plays where she is noted as a performer include Ethan Frome, Elves and the Shoemaker, Shadow and Substance, The Imaginary Invalid, and Suppressed Desires.

Wanda Nelles.bio: Wanda Nelles was a student in the summer of 1945 where she took Weaving with Anni Albers.

Richard Negro Amelar.bio: Richard Negro was a student from 1947 to 1949. He took Weaving with Anni Albers in fall of 1948.

H. Hardin.bio: Grady Hardin taught bible studies at the college for spring 1944. There isn't much online about Hardin, though you can find books he authored about spirituality and religion; titles including Leadership of Worship and The celebration of the gospel: A study in Christian worship.

Richard Lippold.bio: Richard Lippold was guest faculty of sculpture in the summer of 1948. Lippold was an American sculptor, known for his geometric constructions using wire as a medium. His faculty file at Western Regional Archive holds the syllabus for his taught courses, working in metal and wood.

Judith \"Judy\" Chernoff.bio: Judith was a student from the fall of 1944 to the summer of 1946. She took a range of coursework in math, chemistry, "The Bible as a Human Document" psychology, and drama. She was a student officer and participated in at least one play,

Paul Matthen.bio: Paul Matthen was an American bass-baritone, musical scholar and music pedagogue. He was guest in the fall of 1949 to perform at a Bach festival put on by Erwin Bodky. He performed with the State Opera of Stuttgart, Germany, was faculty at Boston University.

Lilian Berger.bio: Lilian Berger attended the 1944 Music Institute. She was a music major at Brooklyn College and a piano teacher at the time of submitting her application.

Elizabeth \"Betty\" Schmitt.bio: Elizabeth “Betty” Schmitt Jennerjahn came to the college for the 1944 art institute and continued on as a student until 1945, and returned from 1948 to 1951 as a student teacher.

Harvey Lichtenstein.bio: Harvey Lichtenstein was a student in the summer of 1952 to take dance with Merce Cunningham.

Mark Wollner.bio: Mark Wollner was a musical guest in 1939. He is listed as violinist on a concert poster for November, 30th, 1939.

Harold \"Larry\" Hatt.bio: Larry was a student for the summer of 1951. He focused in typography and participated in print for the BMC review.

Ruth Hyland.bio: Ruth Hyland was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute.

William \"Bill\" Reed.bio: William Reed was a student from 1936 to 1940. He was also listed as an apprentice teacher for 1941 Spring, 1941 Fall, and 1946 Summer Session.

Marion \"Mary\" Rice.bio: Mary A. Marshall (June 14, 1921–October 15, 1992) represented Arlington County in the House of Delegates from 1966 to 1969 and again from 1972 until 1991. After studying political science at Swarthmore College, from which she graduated with honors, she worked for the U.S. Department of Justice during World War II.

Emery Whipple.bio: Emery Whipple was a student from 1937 to 1940.

Annelise \"Anni\" Albers.bio: Annelise Elsa Freida Fleischmann was born in Berlin, Germany in 1899 and grew up in a comfortable well-to-do family. Her father worked as a furniture maker. Intrigued with design and aesthetics at an early age, she became interested in the idea of becoming an artist. In 1922, she enrolled at the Bauhaus in Weimar. Although originally interested in painting, she was steered towards textiles, as were most women.

Robert \"Bob/ Red\" Abell.bio: Robert Abell shared in his application to Black Mountain College that he applied because he wished to study further away from home. In a recommendation letter from Teresa Foley on January 3, 1946, “In my opinion Robert Abell is exceptionally well adapted to the life and objectives of Black Mountain College. He has spoken to me several times about his desire to study there and I know that he thoroughly understands and is enthusiastic about the philosophy of the College.”

Aristide Mavridis.bio: Aristide Mavridis was a guest on the work camp in the summer of 1942.

Clemens Sandresky.bio: Clemens Sandresky was a guest at the college in the spring of 1946. He was a concert pianist and did a concert at BMC.

Helen Livingston.bio: Helen Livingston taught drama in the summer of 1948. A college bulletin from that summer session shared her courses as "Helen Livingston of the Neighborhood Playhouse in New York City will teach Acting, Speech, and Stagecraft."

Francine DuPlessix.bio: Francine was a student in the summer of 1951.

Layton Noel, Jr..bio: Layton Noel, Jr. was a student in the fall of 1944. He was also a documented visitor in spring of 1946.

James \"Jim\" Leven.bio: James "Jim" Leven was a student for the summer of 1948. Jim and Graham Hamilton came to BMC to study architecture with Edgar Kaufmann.

Samuel \"Sam\" Schecter.bio: Samuel Schecter was a student for the 1945 Summer Music Institute.

Helen Boyden.bio: Helen Boyden taught Economics at the college from the founding semester of fall 1933 to summer of 1935. She was noted to take a leave of absence for 1935-1936. Upon leaving BMC, she took a job at Sarah Lawrence.

James Caldwell.bio: James was a student at the college for the spring 1947 semester.

David Corkran.bio: David H Corkran taught American History at the college from winter of 1945 to summer of 1950 with leave of absence throughout his tenure.

Jane Robinson Stone.bio: Jane Robinson Stone was a student from 1940 to 1944. While a student she was active in many plays, served as a student officer, and married a fellow student.

Alberta Halstead.bio: Alberta Halstead enrolled at Black Mountain College for the 1944 Summer Music Institute on the recommendation of Eduard Steuermann, who was teaching for the summer.

Charles Burchard.bio: Charles Burchard was a guest faculty member in the summer of 1948, teaching architecture.

Adam Atkin.bio: Adam Kissin Atkin was a student at the college from the summer of 1949 to the spring of 1951. In Adam's application, he stated that he was interested in becoming a teacher of mathematics or a mathematician.

Sue Burton.bio: Sue Burton was a student from the fall of 1944 to spring of 1945. She took coursework in art and design, and small house design with Wood. She was interested in attended school for architecture after leaving BMC and shared in a letter to Herbert Miller (In Sue Brown's student file, Brown to Miller, 9/6/1945) that she was working in a small architecture firm in an administrative role.

Felix Krowinski.bio: Felix Thomas Krowinski, Sr., a native of Niagara Falls, New York, graduated from the Buffalo State Hospital School of Nursing in 1943. He served in the U.S. Army during World War II and then attended Black Mountain College for the 1947-1948 regular term and the 1948 summer session.

Joel Oppenheimer.bio: Joel Oppenheimer was a student from spring 1949 to fall 1953. Before BMC he attended Cornell University, School of Engineering, September 1947- June 1948, University of Chicago, September 1948- December 1948, and The Art Students League, New York, September 1949 to present.

Elizabeth \"Betty\" Kaiser.bio: Betty Kaiser was a student at the college from 1953 to 1954. She had an affair with Charles Olson while a student. While at Black Mountain, she had Olsen's child, named Charles Peter Olson. Kaiser became Olson's second common-law wife following his separation from Constance Wilcock in 1956.

Lou \"Barney\" Voigt.bio: Lou Bernard Voigt received his B.S. in 1939 from the University of Illinois and then enrolled at the School of Design at Harvard University where he receive his Master of Landscape Architecture degree.

Virginia \"Ginger\" Osbourne.bio: Virginia Osbourne was a student at the college from 1943 to 1944 where she took Weaving with Anni Albers. She also participated in the student-run maintenance crew and the entertainment committee.

Mervin Lane, Jr..bio: Mervin Lane was a student from fall 1946 to spring 1948. He's well known for his book on BMC called "Sprouted Seeds," among many other works.

Richard \"Dick/ Rick\" Amero.bio: Richard Amero spent his childhood in Gloucester, Massachusetts, where his father, a second-generation French Canadian from Nova Scotia, was a carpenter. His father was eager for him to break with the traditional family trade and deliberately “kept [him] as far away from the tools – carpenter tools – as he could.”

John Collett.bio: John attended in late 1942 to spring 1943. He was born and raised in Norway and worked in New York before coming to BMC and was working to get American citizenship. No transcripts are shared in his file, but a report of treason was filed because he cancelled his citizenship application after learning that he could be drafted.

Henry Gibson.bio: Henry was a student from fall 1948 to summer 1949.

Hans Rademacher.bio: Hans Adolph Rademacher was a German-born American mathematician, known for work in analytic number theory, mathematical genetics, and the theory of functions of a real variable and quantum theory.

Ilona von Karolyi.bio: Ilona von Karolyi was a student from fall 1948 to spring 1949. Before BMC she attended the Cambridge School of Design, September 1947-May 1948.

Richard \"Dick\" Roberts.bio: Richard Roberts was a student and listed as staff in 1947. While at the college, he worked on printing and distributing the college bulletins.

Basil \"Baz\" King.bio: Basil King was a student at the college from 1951 until 1956.

Aaron Siskind.bio: Aaron Siskind was guest faculty of photography in the summer of 1951. System for 25 years, and began photography when he received a camera as a wedding gift and began taking pictures on his honeymoon. He was involved in the abstract expressionism movement.

Eleanore Archer.bio: Eleanore Joicely Archer was a student at the college from the summer of 1949 to the spring of 1950. She left the spring semester after three weeks to be with her mother in Seattle as she just returned from a trip to Korea. She first studied at Stephens College, for the focus of acting and took a range of coursework at Black Mountain, including classes in drama.

Felix Payant.bio: Felix Payant was a writer and editor for "Design." He was a guest at the college in spring of 1946, and was also listed as a donor for the 1946 Summer Institutes and a guest instructor. He created a special issue of Design, published April, 1946, vol. 47 no. 8.

John \"Jack\" Cannon.bio: John Cannon was a student from the fall of 1949 to spring of 1950. He took Weaving courses with Ellen Siegel both semesters that he was at the college.

Oliver Freud.bio: Oliver Freud was guest faculty of geography, physics, and mathematics for the summer of 1943.

Gerda Hagendorn.bio: Gerda was a student from fall 1944 to spring 1946. While a student, she also worked in the registrar's office.

Hope Stephens.bio: Hope Stephens was a student from fall 1935 to spring 1940, where she graduated with Marcel Breuer as her examiner.

Arthur Penn.bio: Arthur Hiller Penn was an American filmmaker, theatre director, and producer. He was a Tony Award winner, and was nominated for three Academy Awards for Best Director, as well as a BAFTA Award, a Golden Globe, two Primetime Emmys.

Joan Keiser.bio: Joan Keiser was a student from 1944 to 1945. She participated in drama productions, such as Titus Maccius Plautus.

Katharine Nipps.bio: Katherine Nipps was a student from fall 1935 to spring 1937. Before BMC she attended White Plains High School 1932-1935.

Martha Davis.bio: Martha Davis King was a student for the summer of 1956.

Theodore \"Ted\" Hines.bio: Theodore Hines was a guest for the work program in 1943 and stayed on for some of spring 1944. While at the college, he participated in a reading of two plays and other drama involvement, such as

Margaret Cole.bio: Margaret was a secretary for the 1944-1945 school year and a student for the summer of 1947, where she took Weaving with Franziska Mayer. She held a BS in library science from Drexel University and took coursework in art and weaving from Berea College and Temple University before attended BMC.

Harrison Begay.bio: Harrison Begay was a student for the 1940-1941 school year under a scholarship from the Indian Commission. Harrison spoke with the Director of Education at the US Department of the Interior, Office of Indian Affairs, and shared that he wanted to "master the White man's culture, while remaining Indian." Though, he shared that he was not interested in furthering training in his arts, but he wanted to learn more English and about a culture outside of his own. Begay also taught a Navajo class while a student.

Florence Kawa.bio: Florence Kawa was a student for the 1944 Summer Art Institute for "only one week" and returned for fall.

José \"Pepe\" Gonzalez y Zayas.bio: Jose was a student from fall 1946 to summer 1948.

Ellsworth \"E.E.\" Dwight, Jr..bio: Ellsworth was a student from fall 1933 to spring 1934.

Janet Seaton.bio: Janet Seaton was a guest for the work program in 1943.

Wilhelm \"Willo\" von Moltke.bio: Willo von Moltke studied at the Technische Hochschule in Berlin where he received his Dipl. Ing. Arch. in 1937. In the spring and summer of 1940, von Moltke worked for Alva Aalto in New York City, and in the fall of 1940, for Oscar Stonorov in Philadelphia. It was at Stonorov’s home that he met Xanti Schawinsky, a former Bauhaus student who had taught at Black Mountain.

Karl With.bio: Karl With was an art historian. With was guest faculty for the Summer Art Institute of 1945.

Eric Bentley.bio: Eric Russell Bentley taught classes in social science, history, drama, and dramatic literature at the college in the summer of 1942, and from spring of 1943 to summer of 1944. While faculty, he also sat on the Library Committee, the Campaign Publicity Committee, and the Membership Committee.

Walter Gropius.bio: Walter Gropius, educator, architect and founder of the Bauhaus, fled Germany for England where he worked with Maxwell Fry and the Isokon Group in London. In 1937, he accepted an invitation to teach architecture at the Graduate School of Design at Harvard University. From 1938-52 he was Chairman of the Department of Architecture.

James Luntz.bio: James Luntz was a student in the fall of 1936 to summer 1937.

Henry \"Hank\" Bergman.bio: Henry Porter Bergman was a student at the college from 1945 to 1947, including involvement in the 1946 Summer Art Institute. While a student, he also worked as an Apprentice Teacher in Woodworking, Mechanics, and Architecture. He was also a Student Officer, sat on the Board of Fellows, and was involved in the Discipline Committee.

Marie McCall.bio: Marie McCall was a student in fall of 1944.

Mark Brunswick.bio: Mark Brunswick was a guest faculty in music for the summer of 1944.

Marilyn \"Widget\" Bauer.bio: Marilyn Jean Bauer, lovingly called “Widget” by friends and professors, was a student at the college from the fall of 1941 to the summer of 1945. Bauer was regularly involved in play productions and costume design and is noted in many playbills and college bulletins for her contributions.

John Chamberlain.bio: John Chamberlain was a student at the college from the summer of 1955 to spring of 1956. He was interested in sculpture and while a student he also worked as an apprentice teacher at the college.

Frederic \"Fred\" Goldsmith.bio: Frederic Goldsmith (1925-2009) followed his sister Nell Goldsmith to Black Mountain College. Both Goldsmiths had attended a progressive school at Milwaukee State Teachers College. After serving in the army, Goldsmith received his B.S. degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He worked at the Clasmann Corporation, the family business which sold products to the power industry, heating/ventilating equipment, and air conditioning equipment.

Laddie Marshack.bio: Laddie Marshack was a student in spring of 1944.

Edgar Konsberg.bio: Edward Konsberg was a student in 1945.

William Brown.bio: William Brown was a student from fall of 1946 to spring of 1947. He applied while in the Army, awaiting discharge, and was interested in taking art courses. His student file shows that he intended to transfer to Cooper Union College upon leaving BMC.

John Lewis.bio: John Lewis was a student in 1950.

James Stokely.bio: James Stokely and his wife Wilma were Asheville locals that audited classes in the fall of 1944.

Harriet Engelhardt.bio: Harriet Engelhardt grew up in a prominent Montgomery, Ala.,family. She attended the Margaret Booth School in Montgomery and later went to Hollins College and Black Mountain College. During World War II she became a Red Cross worker in Europe. She was the driver of a clubmobile which closely followed U. S. troops across France, Germany, and Austria in 1944 and 1945. She was killed in October 1945 in a jeep accident the day before she was scheduled to return to the United States.

John \"Jack\" Kasik.bio: John Kasik was a student in fall of 1940.

Bernard \"Bernie\" Karp.bio: Bernard Karp was a student from 1947 to 1949. While a student, he served as a student officer and participated in community council.

Donald \"Don\" Richter.bio: Donald Louis “Don” Richter attended Black Mountain College in the summer of 1949, as one of Buckminster Fuller’s “Twelve Disciples”, a group of students who had studied with Fuller the previous year at the Institute of Design in Chicago.

Edith Winifred Vail.bio: Edith Vail taught music for small children at BMC for the 1945-1946 school year.

Sue \"Susie\" Schauffler.bio: Sue Schauffler was a student from 1944 to 1945. While a student, she served as a student officer, and participated in the hydrant crew and entertainment committee.

Priscilla Huntington.bio: Priscilla Huntington was a work camp guest for the summer of 1942.

Marcella Martin.bio: Marcella Martin was a student from 1933 to 1935. While a student, she served as a student officer.

Ernst Krenek.bio: Ernst Heinrich Krenek was an Austrian, later American, composer. He explored atonality and other modern styles and wrote a number of books, including Music Here and Now, a study of Johannes Ockeghem, and Horizons Circled: Reflections on my Music. Krenek wrote two pieces using the pseudonym Thornton Winsloe.

Donald \"Don\" Alter.bio: Donald Alter shared in his application, “by attending Black Mountain College I hope to help myself become more mundane. I hope to become more independent in my thinking and living. I also believe it is important for an individual to learn of his relation with cooperative community life. In the final analysis I believe that all the things I hope to gain at Black Mountain would help me to become a more aware and more worthwhile artist. From the information I have gathered about Black Mountain I have concluded that the program offered is conductive to the afore said.”

Hazel Larsen Archer.bio: Hazel Larsen Archer experienced life at BMC as a student, faculty, and as a staff member working in the college office. She studied art, design, and photography, taking classes with Josef Albers, Josef Breitenbach, and Beaumont Newhall among others. Starting in 1949, Hazel was appointed to teach photography, and was at the college for nine years altogether. As many of her students later stated, Hazel had a lasting impact on them with her emphasis on seeing rather than technique. She also invited photographers to teach at Black Mountain College including Harry Callahan, Aaron Siskind, and Arthur Siegel for a special focus on photography in the summer of 1951.
